#1814. Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli needs a statement win to change the narrative around his new-look side

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:37 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 13:37 EST, 15 November 2026

While it’s fair to state that the touchpaper has yet to be lit on Sebastien Pocognoli’s tenure, he is hardly the first Scotland manager to discover that the battle for hearts and minds can be a drawn-out affair.

Although Steve Clarke marked the start of his era with an unconvincing win over Cyprus at Hampden in 2019, the Ayrshireman lost his next four games to Russia and Belgium. It would take him 15 months to chalk up what might be considered a statement victory.

That 2-1 win against the Czech Republic in Olomouc in September 2020, in his tenth match in charge, felt like a turning point for the national team and so it proved with qualification for the delayed Euros in the post. But Clarke certainly had to suffer for it.

So for all the frustration felt at Pocognoli’s new-look side failing to hit the straps in the past five matches, we have been here before. And statistically, to date, it’s also been by no means disastrous.

Notwithstanding how ordinary North Macedonia are, the Belgian is actually the first manager since Gordon Strachan in 2013 to win more than one of his first five games in charge. The history books show that Scotland don’t really do fast starts when there’s a new man at the helm.

Nonetheless, it would be hard to overstate the significance of Pocognoli seeing it all spectacularly come together as the Nations League campaign concludes in St Gallen tomorrow.

Scotland captain Andy Robertson and John McGinn enjoy a light-hearted moment in training.

Sebastien Pocognoli is one of many Scotland managers who have made slow starts in the job.

Switzerland boss Murat Yakin will give some of his fringe players a chance against Scotland.

Friday’s win over the group whipping boys was certainly deserved, yet the performance, particularly in the first half, was hardly scintillating.

Even those who are prepared to be patient with Pocognoli would have been concerned at the lack of tempo and imagination in the general play in the first period.

Weren’t we told that he would bring a radically different approach to Clarke? Yet there was scant evidence on show of the ultra-offensive, high-pressing style which was billed in the brochure.

While a markedly better second half yielded a welcome first home win for the 39-year-old, no one left the arena clicking their heels at what they’d witnessed. This remains very much a work in progress.

What can be said with some certainty, however, is that the players are on board with the grand plan. When they faced the media last week, it was noticeable that Scott McTominay, Andy Robertson and John McGinn all praised the new man’s methods and ideas and predicted that they will bear fruit in the fullness of time.

You get a sense when experienced players are reading empty platitudes from a prepared script. Yet the words of the leadership group felt truly authentic on that occasion.

While Pocognoli will obviously have welcomed them, it’s not statements of support from senior figures which he needs to keep the Tartan Army onside. It’s positive results.

Come what may against Switzerland tomorrow, Scotland don’t have a match until March. That’s an awful long time to reflect if it doesn’t go well.

What Pocognoli and the travelling fans wouldn’t give for that seismic win to shift the narrative and engender a greater sense of optimism ahead of the Euro qualifiers.

Strachan’s first big scalp arrived at the fourth time of asking when a Robert Snodgrass goal sealed an unlikely win away to Croatia. Such unexpected outcomes can have a galvanising effect.

Friday’s narrow win over North Macedonia did keep the possibility alive of Scotland finishing second in Group B1, but few would be sticking their house on that yet coming to pass.

With head-to-head rather than goal difference counting if sides are locked on the same number of points, Pocognoli’s men must beat the Swiss then hope that Slovenia don’t win in Skopje. Stranger things have happened, but not too many.

In all likelihood, Scotland will finish third and be a pot three team when the draw for Euro 2028 is made in Belfast on December 6. Yet, it’s still vital that they conclude this campaign with – at the very least – a display which offers grounds for optimism.

This was always going to be the toughest assignment of the six. In the summer, the Swiss reached the last eight of the World Cup for the first time since 1954, only losing in extra-time to Argentina. That remains their only defeat this year.

They’ve hardly missed a beat in the Nations League, winning four games and drawing one, to comfortably secure promotion to the top tier.

Even though they were given a helping hand by Jack Hendry’s early red card as they won 3-0 at Hampden in September, they looked a level above Pocognoli’s men.

‘We reached all of our goals,’ said coach Murat Yakin.

‘Maybe we could have done even more at the World Cup, but we created history by reaching the quarter-finals.

‘I am happy with our playing style. There’s been good development and we have integrated new players.’

The hope for Scotland stems from the fact that Yakin is compelled to give some fringe players an opportunity to shine in St Gallen.

Inter Milan’s Manuel Akanji has become the latest big name to withdraw through injury. Johan Manzambi, Dan Ndoye and Granit Xhaka were already out.

Even then, the task for the visitors remains formidable. The only defeat for the Swiss in their past 11 games on home soil came at the hands of Germany.

‘It has happened a few times already,’ Yakin said of the injury situation.

‘But we will make sure we get a good level of players on to the pitch. It’s a good thing we have won the group already. It’s now an opportunity to make changes.

‘It doesn’t make sense to wait. We have enough opportunities and possibilities.’

It feels like a night for Pocognoli to proceed with caution. A fairly assured display against North Macedonia means Ryan Porteous, Luke Graham and Kieran Tierney will probably be asked to go again as a back-three.

Given his defensive diligence, Aaron Hickey would be favoured to displace Ben Gannon-Doak on the right flank.

As on Friday, Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson should play behind John McGinn and Scott McTominay with Che Adams leading the line.

On the occasion when he’ll become Scotland’s most capped player with 103 appearances, it’s to be hoped Andy Robertson has a night to remember.

‘What can I say about him?’ added Yakin. ‘He’s a fantastic player, who has also constantly carried the team or the nation of Scotland.

‘The best players should be on the pitch and we’re happy to compete with him. It’s a nice mark for him, and in that sense, congratulations.’

#1813. Nations League draw in full as England, Wales, Republic of Ireland learn fates

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 11:28, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 11:47

England will play Norway in the quarter-finals of the UEFA Nations League.

The Three Lions progressed to the last eight as League A Group 3 winners, having collected 15 points from six matches, including a sensational 3-2 win over Spain on the final matchday.

England's first-placed status meant that they entered the draw as one of the four seeded quarter-finalists, alongside France, Germany and Portugal, while they were unable to be drawn against Spain having already faced them in the group stage.

Thomas Tuchel's side will therefore do battle with Erling Haaland's Norway, who finished as runners-up to Portugal in League A Group 4 and will be seeking revenge for their World Cup 2026 quarter-final defeat to England.

Should England prevail in their reunion with the Scandinavians, they will clash with either Belgium or Germany in the semi-finals, for the right to contest a heavyweight showpiece event.

?????????? Thomas Tuchel's #ThreeLions will face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in March! https://t.co/TQBDCd9I4i

The headline quarter-final sees reigning world and European champions Spain square off with France, a repeat of the 2020-21 Nations League final which Les Bleus won 2-1.

Whoever wins that clash of the titans will pit their wits against either the Netherlands or Portugal, who also squared off in the final of the inaugural Nations League in 2019; the Selecao triumphed 1-0 thanks to a Goncalo Guedes strike.

The first legs of the Nations League quarter-finals will take place between March 25 and March 27, before the return fixtures are held across March 28 and March 30.

England will travel to Norway for their first clash, before welcoming the Nordic nation to Wembley for the return fixture. The semi-finals and final will then be held in June in an as yet undetermined host nation.

Meanwhile, the Republic of Ireland will take on Croatia in the League A/League B playoffs for the right to earn promotion to the top tier, while Wales must beat Slovenia to retain their League A status.

Wales finished bottom of League A Group 4 on three points, but survived automatic relegation to the second division thanks to their superior points total to Turkey and the Czech Republic (both 0).

The Dragons have only ever faced Slovenia once before, drawing 0-0 in a 2005 international friendly.

Ireland's runners-up finish in League B Group 3 means that they have the chance to rise to League A for the first time ever, having only competed in League B since the Nations League's inception.

The Boys in Green have only beaten Croatia twice in their previous seven meetings, though, and lost 3-1 during their most recent head-to-head at Euro 2012.

#1812. Charlotte aiming to take goal-scoring momentum into Chicago clash

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Dean Smith believes Charlotte FC have the ability to ride their end-of-season momentum in front of goal as they prepare for another campaign in the MLS Cup playoffs.

Charlotte signed off the regular season with an entertaining 3-3 draw with Inter Miami, with the Crown coming from three goals down to claim a point at Nu Stadium.

Liel Abada's brace and Rodolfo Aloko's 90th-minute leveller ensured a share of the spoils, though Charlotte were pipped to fourth place by the Chicago Fire in the process.

And that is who they will face in their Round One best-of-three series, with the first match coming this weekend at SeatGeek Stadium against Gregg Berhalter's side.

But Charlotte come into the match off the back of an unbeaten three-game run, a stretch that saw them plunder 11 goals, with eight of those coming in 4-0 routs over Orlando City SC and CF Montreal.

"I'm disappointed because we were aiming for a top four finish," Smith said. "If we had beaten Miami last time out, we would have found ourselves in that top four.

"I'm proud of the boys, though. There has been a lot of change this year. We've brought new players in during that time and I think we have grown overall as a team.

"You have seen from the World Cup break how much we have grown, and we will go into the playoffs knowing that we can certainly go and cause problems and score goals.

"We ended the season with 11 goals in three games and going into the playoffs, we know we have got that behind us. And we've got two clean sheets as well, so we've got momentum at both ends of the pitch, so I'm looking forward to it."

We're done waiting. #CrownsUp https://t.co/Wgd9Cd7ZcM

— Charlotte FC (@CharlotteFC) November 20, 2026

Chicago are, however, another side in rich goal-scoring form. Their final regular-season match saw them go down 4-3 to the Columbus Crew, though they still sealed fourth.

The Fire have not appeared in an MLS Cup final since 2003, when they lost to San Jose Earthquakes.

They also lost in the 2000 final to the Kansas City Wizards, and their only MLS Cup success came 28 years ago, when they defeated D.C. United 2-0 in the 1998 final.

If anyone in Chicago's squad knows about winning major trophies, then Lewandowski is certainly the man for the big occasion.

Lewandowski has managed nine goals and five assists in 19 appearances since leaving Barcelona, and he will be keen to lead Chicago to glory here.

But Charlotte have their own creative midfield maestro in Biel, who leads the MLS for assists so far this season (18).

The Spaniard also has 10 goals for Charlotte, while his 65 chances created rank as the most of any player within Smith's ranks this season in MLS.

— Charlotte FC (@CharlotteFC) November 19, 2026

Despite being favoured by the Opta supercomputer, Charlotte have failed to win any of their last four meetings with Chicago in the MLS, losing all four. The Fire during that period have outscored their opponents 10-4.

Indeed, Charlotte's last win away at Chicago came back in May 2024, when Ashley Westwood, who looks likely to start this weekend, scored the only goal in the 60th minute.

Smith's side also struggled on their travels last year, only managing five road wins throughout the regular season, while Chicago picked up nine home victories, a tally only seven teams across both divisions could better.

#1811. ESPN Brasil: Real Madrid open to permanent Endrick sale – Milan have ‘two aces’ to play

Another source in Endrick’s homeland Brazil have gone big with the story that a permanent move to AC Milan is possible.

This morning, we relayed the news from TNT Sports Brasil, who claimed that Milan are readying a package worth €70m to sign Endrick. They claimed that a loan deal is now ‘off the table’ and that a winter switch is possible on a permanent basis.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Now, further confirmation has arrived from ESPN Brasil. They state that Real Madrid want €60-70m in order to sell the young forward, which is the amount that their colleagues at TNT suggested the Rossoneri would offer.

Furthermore, Real Madrid have not ruled out including a buy-back clause in the operation should Endrick reach a high level at San Siro. President Florentino Pérez holds Endrick in high regard, so he fears the regret of losing him.

ESPN adds that neither Real Madrid nor Endrick are considering another loan and are working on the prospect of negotiating a permanent move in January. In all of this, Milan have two ‘aces up their sleeve’, as per the report.

The first is the fact Endrick is represented by ROC Nation. They are an agency that Gerry Cardinale has a good relationship with, and they have expressed a certain ‘fatigue’ towards Los Blancos due to Endrick’s lack of opportunities since returning to the Santiago Bernabéu after his loan at Lyon.

The second ace is that at Milan he would be a key starting player, with a tailor made role for him on the right side of the attack. With this comes the guarantee of more minutes, which could boost his profile also when it comes to the national team.

ESPN report that Jose Mourinho is firm on his stance: he will deploy Endrick when he deems it appropriate and depending on the context of each match or each situation. The manager will continue to prioritise the team over the individual, but wants Endrick to say.

As mentioned, if he is sold then Real Madrid’s desire is to recoup a large portion of the sum invested in his 2022 purchase, when he was still at Palmeiras. At the time, the transfer was finalised for around €70m, including bonuses.

#1810. Legendary commentator CLIVE TYLDESLEY on how his ITV exit has made hearts grow fonder, the rise of YouTube streamers, his lockdown money-spinner - and why he refuses to be another loud voice in the game

Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:00 EST, 15 November 2026

Clive Tyldesley reaches for his glasses as he rummages through the commentary charts crammed into an old filing cabinet, jokes about his fading eyesight and supposes one day he will no longer be able to identify footballers from the gantry.

Fortunately, we are still far from that point. At 72, Tyldesley is calling the game as accurately as ever. His eyes are perfectly good when bespectacled, his mind nimble enough to keep up with play and his soothingly familiar voice strong and authoritative with a gentle tendency towards self-deprecation.

This much was evident as Manchester United roared back to beat Roma in the Champions League and a clip of his spine-tingling commentary from the live CBS broadcast circulated on social media and found an appreciative audience in Europe.

'I don't know if there's an element of nostalgia in hearing my voice again,' says Tyldesley. 'If I'm honest, I've dodged the worst of the public's ire with everything including commentators because I haven't been around for the last few years.

'Absence has made a few hearts grow a little fonder towards me and maybe if I'd been on Sky every week for the last six years, I'd be no less unpopular than anybody else out there. So, I can't pretend it's not nice to get some engagement with an audience I used to commentate to on a regular basis, but I'm very happy where I am.'

Tyldesley has been the lead commentator for the CBS coverage of the Champions League since 2020, converting transfer fees into US dollars and keeping his measurements imperial for a North American audience but otherwise approaching the job as he always did.

Clive Tyldesley is calling the game as accurately as ever at 72 and is 'very happy' in his role as the lead commentator of CBS coverage of the Champions League

Tyldesley's commentary of Man United's comeback against Roma circulated on social media and received an appreciative audience in Europe

The 72-year-old wonders whether there was an element of nostalgia to the reaction, with Tyldesley's work for CBS meaning his commentary cannot be shown in Europe

Clips of the studio panel featuring Thierry Henry, Micah Richards, Jamie Carragher and presenter Kate Scott are popular on social media but live action featuring Tyldesley's commentary is governed by broadcasting rights deals and cannot be shown in Europe.

The one from Old Trafford of Matheus Cunha's winning goal in the 86th minute slipped through the net on X and reminded everyone his passion for football is undimmed, and his voice can still stand hairs on attention.

'I don't think I've seen a better game than the first leg of the Paris Saint-Germain v Bayern Munich Champions League semi-final,' says Tyldesley on the rare quality of Europe's elite competition. 'I listened to people with hundreds more England caps than me saying it was bad defending, but I watched the whole game back the next day and it wasn't.

'I'm sorry but it was wonderful attacking and a show of intent by two coaches who trusted defenders to defend one-on-one and attackers to score more than the opposition. Rob Green was my co-commentator and at the end we just put our microphones down and looked at each other and said, "Wow."

'I've not forgotten muddy pitches and assassin centre backs. You only need to look on YouTube to see football was different, but you can't pretend it was better. I see terrible games today just as I did then, but particularly in the Champions League, I regularly stumble upon football that gets me off my seat.'

His exit from ITV, first displaced by Sam Matterface as lead commentator in 2020 and then released entirely after Euro 2024 clearly smarted but Tyldesley is comfortable as the veteran in the fast-changing media landscape.

'Most of the principles I picked up from watching John Motson, Barry Davies and Brian Moore in their pomp are applicable to commentary in 2026,' he says. 'There's no need to reinvent that particular wheel.

'You can offer alternatives such as fan zones and screaming watchalongs for people to view it in a different way. I make it my business to look at J_Tekkz or LDN Movements or whatever is pulling in millions on YouTube.

Tyldesley believes he has not seen a better game than the first leg of PSG's Champions League semi-final with Bayern Munich last year

The veteran commentator believes most of the principles he learned starting out still apply, but admits to having watched popular new voices to see if anything could apply to his commentary

Tyldesley also works as a guest lecturer and commentates for blockbuster computer games, as well as selling framed prints of his commentary charts

'I sample a bit of Mark Goldbridge to see why he's prominent but I'm hearing nothing in those guys applicable to the way I call a football match so I carry on with the same focus I've always had on what constitutes good commentary.'

The central principle being that the game is bigger than the individuals in it, he points out, with viewers tuning in for the football not the commentator.

'The biggest challenge for a television commentator is to find the right words at the big moments, to go beyond "amazing," "brilliant", "incredible" and try to add some editorial context,' says Tyldesley.

'Every goal is unique. The words following a goal that is going to be remembered for years should be unique and specific to that goal, but that's difficult to do. It's unscripted performance and difficult to master and capture.

'I am concentrating hardest for the 10-15 seconds after a big goal because I'm searching for words which will become a small part of people's memories. That's very different to consciously trying to provide 45-second soundbites to amplify one's own personality and standing on social media.

'There's a danger of media leaning that way as it develops such an emphasis on the bitesize.'

Among other things, Tyldesley is a guest lecturer for media students at the University of Salford, still doing commentaries for blockbuster computer games and selling framed prints of his commentary charts, something that started as 'a silly idea in lockdown'.

His wife Susan bought a dozen frames to see how it went. Originally, he offered three Champions League finals won by English clubs in 1999, 2005 and 2012. He sent one each to Gary Neville who played for Manchester United in 1999 and Jamie Carragher who played for Liverpool in 2005. They both posted images online and demand skyrocketed.

'Two good friends,' smiles Tyldesley. 'I probably got about half a million pounds of free advertising out of them.' Sales have soared beyond 50,000. There's a Celtic chart on the gym in Rod Stewart's house. Ant and Dec have bought signed Newcastle charts.

His own venture into podcasting was short-lived and he politely declines between five and ten invitations each week to appear on others.

'I've tried to step back from that kind of thing,' says Tyldesley. 'So much content I hear on football is empty, verbose and repetitive. Really, there are only so many things you can say about Alexander Isak having his shirt pulled in mid-air and Gary Neville probably said most of them in the 30 seconds following the incident.

Tyldesley has no plans to retire and Paramount, the owners of his employers CBS - and soon to be the owners of TNT Sports - will have the UK rights for the Champions League

Sales of his framed commentary charts, something that started during lockdown, have soared beyond 50,000

'There are so many brutally judgmental loud voices in and around football attracting attention that I want to be as far away from as possible, so that's what I do. Unless I sense an opportunity to talk about communication and broadcasting rather than whether club A, B or C should replace their manager. That's not for me Clive.'

So, there's a little less Tyldesley out there than there was. He was content to stay at home and watch the World Cup from his sofa this summer for the first time since 1990.

But there are no plans to retire. And who knows what might change next season when Paramount, the owners of CBS – and soon to be the owners of current rights holders TNT Sports – have the UK rights for the Champions League.

There might be a familiar voice beamed into our living rooms once again.

When I saw the Dear England play, I was the only person in the theatre who didn't enjoy it, and that was because I hated the portrayal of Harry Kane.

He was written as an uneducated numbskull. Written to laugh at and the theatre laughed at him. He was stupid and gullible, another thick footballer.

And anyone who has spent time with footballers will know they might lack for an Eton College education but are streetwise and invariably smart with a razor sharp sense of humour.

Kane is a leader of those men. There's not a single thing about the person Kane has made himself to laugh or sneer at and I wanted to stand up in the theatre that afternoon and shout at everyone.

Oddly, I was introduced to the playwright James Graham at a function a few weeks later and he kind of pushed me for my opinion of Dear England.

I tried to be diplomatic, but I felt so strongly I ended up scolding him for writing a character called Harry Kane who was nothing like Harry Kane.

So, that was the end of a beautiful friendship before it began. And I'm so thrilled now there's a better appreciation of the person Harry is.

#1808. Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty

Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?

It is important, first and foremost, to explain this is not painting a narrative about Liverpool being unfortunate. Far from it. Iraola hissed his dismay that Nottingham Forest had shown more intensity and been the better team for long periods in an entertaining 2-2 draw.

But the penalty that changed the contest? Iraola, his coaching staff, even the supporters behind the dugout had been left flabbergasted that the malfunctioning number board of fourth official Tim Robinson presented an avenue for Forest to exploit.

Iraola had tried to make a triple change, wanting to introduce Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha, but as Robinson pressed buttons to no avail and everyone in Red became frustrated, Forest substitute Liam Delap took a quick throw and the Liverpool house almost caved in.

Neco Williams, once of Liverpool, surged into the penalty area, Alisson Becker arrived a fraction too late after the defender got his shot away and took his old team-mate down. Morgan Gibbs-White exacerbated the damage when sending Alisson the wrong way and this was the last thing a manager wanting to make an impression on a big day needed to see but this was reality.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

“I cannot explain because I don’t have an explanation,” Iraola said. “I wanted to make those substitutions about three minutes before. I mean, it was two, three, four times the ball had gone out. I still don’t know the reason why we couldn’t make the subs.

“I think [the fourth official] was having some problems with the board or something. It [the penalty] wouldn’t have happened if I had made the sub. I asked. I had complained the previous time. The supporters were shouting and they were aware of the situation. But I don’t know what happened and I don’t know why they have given the penalty.”

"A professional fourth official cannot take three minutes." 😳Andoni Iraola was not happy with the time taken to get the substitutes' board ready.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fMfYOjQJPd

He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

“There were many positive aspects,” said Glasner. “It has been a three-game week; some players played. We are getting more and more fitness, that is just the foundation of how we want to play. It is just a point but it still feels a bit frustrating, so we have to stay humble.”

"I think we were very poor in the first half." 😤Andoni Iraola gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance against Nottingham Forest.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/COZfhwkLeX

Neco Williams and James McAtee react to Nottingham Forest's draw at Anfield 🌳🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BjX0p1yQ1m

"We started the game pretty bad today." 😬Alexander Isak gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance at Anfield.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/3wD0hplmQ6

The playmaker added another goal and assist to his tally this afternoon.

20 - Morgan Gibbs-White has been directly involved in 20 goals in 2026 (15 goals, 5 assists), the joint-most of any Premier League player in all competitions (level with Haaland).His 13 goals in the Premier League in 2026 are also the most of any player.Decisive. pic.twitter.com/p1wQFwXvsI

Liverpool and Forest are both made to wait for their first Premier League wins of the season as the two sides play out a pulsating 2-2 draw at Anfield.

Full-time scenes at Anfield as Liverpool and Nottingham Forest share the points 🤝📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/WqOpfU38es

Sels calmly comes out to claim a deep cross to relieve the pressure on Forest. Munoz runs back to dispossess Delap and win a free kick, giving Liverpool another chance to launch the ball forward.

Glasner makes a very late double change as Hudson-Odoi and Dominguez replace McAtee and Igor Jesus.

There will be five minutes of added time. Liverpool continue their relentless search for a third goal, while Forest are holding on.

It’s wave after wave of Liverpool pressure. Forest are camped inside their own half. Igor Jesus and Delap are chasing every loose ball, but Forest are struggling to get out at the moment.

Munoz’s goal has provided another twist in this pulsating encounter. Isak wins a free kick in such dangerous territory and Szoboszlai steps up to take it. The Hungarian slams a venomous effort wide of the far post. Can either side find a late winner?

What an incredible finish! Wirtz threads a delightful pass through to Munoz. With his back to goal, the winger swivels and takes the ball on the outside of Murillo, before smashing a thunderous effort into the roof of the net, which brushes the crossbar on its way in.

Munoz, take a bow! 🤯👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GD8IAdy2rJ

Igor Jesus does brilliantly to escape Nyoni, before he is pulled to the ground by Arajou, who is booked. It’s been an excellent defensive effort from Forest.

Iraola makes his final two alterations as Araujo and Nyoni replace Jacquet and Mac Allister.  Szoboszlai then swings such an inviting delivery into the penalty area, but Isak miscues his strike with his left foot.

Amid the chaos, Alisson was booked just before the penalty after appealing the decision and Iraola has ordered a triple change, taking off Kerkez, Frimpong and Gakpo for Tsimikas, Gravenberch and Ngumoha. This has seen Szoboszlai move out to right back.

Andoni Iraola is about to make his substitution and this is interesting because he had planned to introduce Rio Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas and Ryan Gravenberch 10 minutes ago but told them to sit down after Liverpool had equalised. Forest have put Liam Delap on, giving him his debut after completing his £45m move to the club.

The Forest captain sends Alisson the wrong way, powering a clinical penalty into the net. Gibbs-White demonstrates fantastic composure and Liverpool have it all to do again.

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

Delap showcases excellent initiative and takes a quick throw-in to send Williams through on goal. Alisson rushes out and catches Williams as he attempts to lob the goalkeeper. Williams crashes to the ground and the referee points to the spot. Alisson is furious. What a chance for Forest to restore their lead.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

This game is being played at a ferocious pace and Forest’s club-record signing Delap enters the action as he replaces Ndoye. Can the former Chelsea striker mark his debut with a much-needed goal?

That leveller has injected so much energy into Liverpool. Anfield believes again. Isak really needed that goal.

So much credit must go to Gakpo. The winger shrugs off Williams and fires a pinpoint cross towards the back post. Isak is there and converts from close range. We’re set up for such an intriguing finale. Liverpool have the momentum now.

Isak equalises for Liverpool at the Kop end! 🔴🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/qKFxq2AqaB

Wirtz’s frustrating afternoon is compounded as he picks up a booking after hauling Murillo to the ground. Iraola looks to be readying some substitutions.

There is a very strange feeling here: it’s almost a case of the home fans waiting for Nottingham Forest to score a second goal rather than anticipating that Liverpool will equalise. The early buzz in the atmosphere has gone and that is because the gaps everyone can see in the make up of the team remain. How Bradley Barcola will transform this situation?

Jacquet’s pass is intercepted and Ndoye is released on the counter. He’s guided out wide by Van Dijk but still squeezes in a brilliant cross. Gibbs-White was running up the pitch in support and slowed down, meaning no one was there to turn in Ndoye’s delivery.

Munoz is the next player to be booked after reacting angrily to a decision. Iraola has to consider making some changes soon.

Aina catches Munoz with a late challenge and he’s the second Forest player to go into the referee’s book.

You can already see in this second half that there is acres of space for Forest to exploit on the counter as Liverpool push for a leveller. Munoz then heads a point-blank header over the bar. Luckily for the Spaniard, the offside flag was up against Gakpo.

We are back for the second half here at Anfield. Can Liverpool find a route back into this game or can Forest hold onto the three points?

It’s a bizarre situation for Liverpool. They could easily be level or be 2-0 down. But they trial just 1-0 at half-time. Wirtz and Gakpo are looking lively, but Isak has struggled to influence the game.

Dan Ndoye scores his first goal in the Premier League in 377 days 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tjSiGoSPyW

Forest have a slender one-goal advantage at the break after a frantic first half at Anfield. Ndoye curled the visitors into a well-deserved lead after 24 minutes, before Wirtz had a goal ruled out for offside. The German was then sensationally denied by Sels’ diving save as he tipped Wirtz’s header over the bar. Alisson then replicated Sels’ heroics, parrying Igor Jesus’ strike against the woodwork to stop Forest from doubling their lead.

What a move and what a save! Murillo sprays an inch-perfect pass out to Aina, who chops inside of Munoz and fires a low cross into Igor Jesus. The Forest striker shoots first-time from inside the penalty area, but his effort is sensationally parried onto the bar by Alisson. That is a world-class stop from the Brazilian goalkeeper.

A world-class save from Alisson denies Forest a second! 🤯🧤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4NtzROILrU

Igor Jesus receives the game’s first yellow card after clipping Mac Allister with an unnecessary challenge.

Liverpool then fly forward again as Gakpo nutmegs Williams. His cross trickles through to Munoz at the back post. The ball is slightly behind Munoz and he leans back before shooting, causing his strike to narrowly sail over the bar.

There will be three minutes of added time to conclude this first half.

Liverpool are applying all the pressure at the end of this first half. At times, Forest have had every outfield player behind the ball.

Sels makes a superb save! Gakpo takes on his marker on the outside and fires in a cross which Wirtz meets. The attacker gets in between Schlager and Aina to win the header, but his effort is excellently tipped over the bar by Sels.

Out of nothing, Liverpool are level. McAtee attempts to play out from a deep position and his pass is intercepted by Wirtz. The ball breaks to Frimpong, who slips a clever pass to Wirtz. The German playmaker swivels and slides a low effort into the bottom corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Frimpong was in an offside position before he provided the assist. VAR confirms this and Liverpool’s joy has been cut short. That is a huge let off for Forest, who need to be more careful with possession in deeper areas.

Following that Forest goal, there was a small flurry of Liverpool pressure, with Szoboszlai having a free kick punched away by Sels. Murillo is then very careless with the ball and is dispossessed. This allowed Mac Allister to play in Isak, but the striker is crowded out by multiple Forest defenders before he can get a shot away.

For the third season in a row, Nottingham Forest lead at Anfield. The goal had been coming, too. Liverpool were bright early but suddenly big gaps have started appearing and Forest are wily enough to exploit. There are lots of gripes around the stands about it being “too easy” and this knowledgeable crowd are right. A long ball forward and a simple flick has caused mayhem.

Forest are ahead and are well worth their lead. Sels launches a long ball up to Igor Jesus, who takes it down with an exquisite touch. The ball then breaks to Gibbs-White. The Forest captain plays in Ndoye and the winger curls a clinical effort into the far bottom corner to send the away support wild.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

Liverpool are struggling to find any space in and around Forest’s midfield and defence. Isak and Wirtz have been on the periphery as the time ticks over midway point of the first half.

Huge chance for Forest! McAtee drops deep and picks out Ndoye with a teasing cross. The forward meets the delivery and his header bounces wide. Upon the replays, there looks to have been a push on Frimpong by Ndoye. The referee’s whistle wasn’t sounded so it would have been interesting to see what would of happened if that chance had been converted.

It’s been a really frantic start to this game. Out of possession, Forest are retreating into a really rigid back five formation. Going forward, Aina and Williams are getting up the pitch at every opportunity.

Aina stands up an inviting cross to the back post for Ndoye, who heads it back into the danger zone. Igor Jesus latches onto it, but Jacquet makes a goal-saving tackle to block the striker’s close-range effort.

Sensational block from Jeremy Jacquet to deny Igor Jesus! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/XuhO1GuE9F

Van Dijk clips a long ball over to the onrushing Isak as Liverpool look to burst forward on the counter. Isak races onto it and enters the penalty area, but he’s chased by Jair Cunha who matches the striker for pace. There’s a shoulder-to-shoulder, and the Forest defender bumps Isak off the ball, before Milenkovic comes back to mop up the danger.

Ndoye attempts to sprint in behind Liverpool’s defence. He’s chased by Jacquet and Ndoye can’t quite take the ball under his spell. That is an early warning sign for Liverpool.

The hosts then go up the other end as Mac Allister threads a delightful pass through to Gakpo. The Liverpool forward tries to swivel and shoot, but Williams tracks back and makes a crucial tackle.

Frimpong gets in behind Forest’s backline and attempts to pick out Gakpo with a cross aimed towards the back post. However, the ball bobbles and the Liverpool right back overhits his delivery.

A very intriguing team selected by Andoni Iraola and one that illustrates his confidence. It could be viewed as big call to drop Ryan Gravenberch and Rio Ngumoha but Victor Munoz and Alexis Mac Allister both made a difference when they were introduced at St James’s Park last Sunday and they warrant their inclusion. Munoz won’t be fit enough to play 90 minutes but it will be fascinating to watch him, particularly as Bradley Barcola will soon arrive to play in the same position on the left flank.

We are now under way at Anfield. Can Iraola mark his first competitive home game with a win or will Glasner get up and running with Forest?

A roaring rendition of You’ll Never Walk Alone has just boomed around Anfield. We will now observe a minute’s applause for Liverpool legend Kevin Keegan, who passed away at the age of 75 in July.

Anfield remembers Kevin Keegan ❤️A special tribute to the Liverpool legend ahead of kick-off. pic.twitter.com/bJgi58vPj7

A very poignant and colourful tribute to Kevin Keegan, with Anfield paying its respects to one of its favourite sons. The atmosphere is good and the onus is on the team to maintain it. This won’t be easy, as Nottingham Forest arrive here with a point to prove under Oliver Glasner. The big story with Forest will come later, with their pursuit of Everton’s Harrison Armstrong. It it is a transfer that is causing huge discussion on Merseyside.

Both sets of players are out onto the pitch and are met by an electric atmosphere at Anfield.

All set for #LIVNFO 💪 pic.twitter.com/IJOZ6NwGNW

Earlier this month, Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group announced they had agreed to sell a minority equity stake to 1892 Holdings, a consortium led and managed by Amit Bhatia, who is in attendance at Anfield today.

On the development, Bhatia told Liverpool’s website: “It feels incredible. It feels surreal when I hear those words, obviously an incredibly proud moment for myself, for my family, for our partners. We’re talking about Liverpool Football Club here, right? I mean, we’re talking about the greatest football club in the world. And so to have the ability to be involved in any capacity is a huge privilege and a huge honour.”

Having been linked to both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City, Cody Gakpo’s Liverpool future has looked doubtful at points this summer.

However, Spurs’ signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush, as well as Manchester City’s potentially big-money pursuit of Enzo Fernandez, means that any exit for the Dutchman looks extremely complicated.

Gakpo scored Liverpool’s first equaliser in their chaotic 2-2 draw with Newcastle United and starts today on the left wing.

❤️ https://t.co/MgbTcQWank pic.twitter.com/DwIooN2OFk

In September 2024, Nottingham Forest claimed their first win over Liverpool at Anfield in 55 years thanks to Callum Hudson-Odoi’s sumptuous 72nd-minute curler.

When Callum Hudson-Odoi made history at Anfield 🤩 pic.twitter.com/HhJ73WztMd

Last season’s emphatic 3-0 victory in the same fixture under Sean Dyche means that Forest have successive wins at a ground where they could notoriously never manage three points.

Nottingham Forest have smashed their club-record transfer fee to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap for £50m on a five-year deal, ending a lengthy pursuit by both the club and their head coach Oliver Glasner.

Last summer Delap held talks with Forest and Glasner, while he was in charge at Crystal Palace, before he opted to join his mentor and former Manchester City Under-21 coach Enzo Maresca at Stamford Bridge.

One of the summer’s most talked about and protracted transfer pursuits is nearing its conclusion as Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal with Paris St-Germain to sign Bradley Barcola.

The Frenchman was absent from PSG’s squad on Friday evening as Luis Enrique’s side drew 2-2 with Lille in Ligue 1.

Barcola is yet another big-money addition to Liverpool’s forward line, following on from the signings of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer.

He also has the approval of club legend Steven Gerrard, who is at Anfield on duty for TNT Sports.

"Incredible talent." 🌟Steven Gerrard reacts to Liverpool's pursuit of Bradley Barcola.🎙️ @OliviaBuzaglo | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/bVd7odopa3

"It was the shared vision." 🤝Oliver Glasner on why he chose to join the Nottingham Forest project 👀 pic.twitter.com/ldxjwU8FW4

"For me, it's a special game, definitely." ❤️Andoni Iraola looks ahead to his first Premier League game at Anfield as Liverpool boss.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fukilMigKz

Liverpool: Alisson, Frimpong, Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez, Szoboszlai, Mac Allister, Munoz, Wirtz, Gakpo, Isak.

Subs: Mamardashvili, Endo, Tsimikas, Araujo, Gravenberch, Nyoni, McConnell, Koumas, Ngumoha.

Nottingham Forest: Sels, Jair Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo, Aina, Schlager, McAtee, Williams, Ndoye, Gibbs-White, Igor Jesus.

Subs: John Victor, Diomande, Hudson-Odoi, Dominguez, Wood, Delap, Yates, Netz, Abbott.

It's good to be back 😍 @Expedia pic.twitter.com/IGv6d9Pbhq

Having only joined up with his teammates a couple of days ago, new signing Liam Delap begins his Nottingham Forest career on the bench, with Igor Jesus preferred as the central striker.

Lining up at Liverpool. 📋 pic.twitter.com/1gtQ7BQz5J

Andoni Iraola has made two changes to the side that drew with Newcastle United. Victor Munoz starts with Rio Ngumoha on the bench. The other alteration sees Alexis Mac Allister replace Ryan Gravenberch in midfield.

Team news is IN! 🔴 #LIVNFO pic.twitter.com/3avoOQOPrM

Anfield will host its first Premier League match of the 2026-27 season.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

This encounter pits two summer appointments – Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner – against each other as they both search for their first top-flight win at their new clubs.

In the opening Premier League game-week, Iraola’s Liverpool needed a last-gasp 99th-minute penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue an unconvincing 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St. James’ Park. Meanwhile, Nottingham Forest have suffered back-to-back home defeats in four days against Leeds United without scoring (1-0 Premier League, 2-0 Carabao Cup).

Iraola has been handed the unenviable task of steering Liverpool back on track following a hugely disappointing campaign under Arne Slot, whose side’s defence of their Premier League ended in a meek fifth-place finish despite spending more than £400m in the previous summer.

The former Bournemouth boss must uncover how to get the best out of big-money recruits such as Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, and also tighten up Liverpool’s vulnerable midfield and defence. Given the pressure of the job and the club’s hectic schedule while balancing domestic and European football, it’s a tough ask. However, Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal for Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola to bolster their attacking reinforcements, but the transfer hasn’t been finalised in time for today’s match.

Last season, Forest endured an equally tumultuous campaign, churning through a staggering four managers, before eventually stumbling to a 16th-place finish. Glasner has been hand-picked by owner Evangelos Marinakis to usher in an era of stability and success, after winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League in just over two years at Crystal Palace.

Both Marinakis and Glasner are extremely ambitious and demanding figures. You’d imagine a top-half finish would be considered the absolute minimum for Forest, while Glasner’s track record of winning trophies surely indicates that Marinakis is eyeing some silverware at the City Ground.

It’s a meeting of two managers who must deliver. Three points for either side would serve as a much-needed tonic to kickstart their seasons.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1807. Under-17 World Cup: Five African wonderkids to watch, including Man United and Chelsea prospects

By Axel Clody | 20 Nov 2026 12:42

With ten representatives at The Under-17 World in Qatar, Africa has several promising generations, with players already noticed at the last Africa Cup of Nations and graduates of prestigious academies. Here are five profiles to watch closely, who could use this event to move up a level.

Some are already considered major figures in their national teams, while others will have the chance to make a name for themselves with the general public and recruiters.

Morocco have several interesting individuals, but Ibrahim Rabbaj is already considered the star of the team. Born in England, the 17-year-old forward plays for Chelsea, where he has gradually climbed the ranks until joining the Under-18 group. Creative, technical and able to play both centrally and on the flank, he has a fine attacking palette. Versatile, he has even occasionally filled in as a left-back at club level!

Already crowned African Under-17 champion with Morocco in 2025, he has been able to gauge the demands of major competitions. Under former international Ahmed Kantari, he will have the chance to confirm that his potential can also be expressed on the world stage.

Algeria return to the Under-17 World Cup for the first time since 2009 and will be able to count on Yacine Abed to lead their attack.

Trained at Paradou AC, the most prolific academy in the country, the forward particularly stood out at the last Under-17 Africa Cup of Nations, where he notably scored twice against South Africa (2-0), helping Algeria’s youngsters take a big step towards qualification.

Quick and technical, Abed has an interesting profile to unsettle opposing defences. This World Cup will be an opportunity to confirm his promise against opposition of a different calibre.

Interesting transfer as Ivorian youth international Harafat Diabaté (2009) ?? has committed to join Celta Vigo, officially signing next January. More on him soon! ? https://t.co/yyhc0ZdCsK

For Ivory Coast, Mohamed Harafat Diabate is a name to remember. The Celta Vigo forward, who joined in July from Racing Club d’Abidjan, could use this competition to make himself stand out. He had already caught the eye at the Under-17 Africa Cup of Nations, notably scoring the winning penalty against DR Congo (1-0) in the final minutes of the match.

Alongside players such as Hubert Yao Kouassi, he represents an additional option for an Ivorian side that is not short of ambition. His ability to be decisive in key moments will be watched particularly closely in Qatar.

Reigning African champions, Senegal have a particularly interesting generation. Among their talents, El Hadji Ibrahima Sow deserves particular attention. A product of AS Dakar Sacre-Coeur, which has produced Pathe Mboup, Alassane Ndao and Iliman Ndiaye, the attacking midfielder is already playing in the Senegalese top flight despite being 16.

His main quality is his vision of the game. Able to find spaces between the lines, deliver passes in the final metres and pose a threat from set pieces, Sow has the profile of a true playmaker. His intelligence and calm in decisive areas could help Senegal, who dream of taking another step after their continental triumph.

Finally, Cameroon will be able to count on Douka Nkoto, a midfielder in the Manchester United academy. Initially trained in Cameroon, at Player FC of Yaounde, he joined the Manchester United academy with his brother Bassirou. Although born in Cameroon, he had started out representing England before being brought back into the Cameroon fold through a step up to the Under-23 side, alongside his brother.

The two players, both born in 2010, are presented as modern midfielders, able to put in repeated efforts, win the ball back and push forward. Douka will notably need to show his ability to manage the rhythm and intensity of an international competition. For Cameroon, who have never yet got past the group stage of an Under-17 World Cup, his contribution in midfield could be valuable.

#1806. Kane sidelined ‘for a few months’ with ankle ligament injury

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Harry Kane has suffered an ankle ligament injury that will keep him out for months, but Vincent Kompany urged Bayern Munich to "try and turn this situation into something positive".

Kane was forced off with the injury just 20 minutes into Bayern's 1-1 draw with Koln on Friday, on their return to Bundesliga action.

And the reigning champions confirmed that Kane was set to be "sidelined for the next few months" with the injury to his left ankle.

German media reports suggested he will be out for three months.

It is a huge blow to Bayern, given the reigning Ballon d'Or winner has 12 goal involvements in the league this season (four goals, eight assists).

Michael Olise also went off against Koln and was subsequently diagnosed with a bruised foot, meaning both he and Kane will join the likes of Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, Ismael Saibari, Alphonso Davies and Manuel Neuer on the sidelines.

Kompany, who has just returned to the dugout himself after recovering from a meningeal irritation that caused him to collapse at Bayern's training ground, admitted his injury list was a cause for concern, but he is determined to be optimistic.

"It was a special match, of course," he said.

"I think we didn't get off to a bad start; we were really in the game and had some pace. But then Harry Kane and Michael Olise suffered injuries, of course.

Harry Kane sustained a syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle during this evening’s home match against 1. FC Köln. This was confirmed by an examination carried out by FC Bayern’s medical department. The 33 year-old will be sidelined for the next few months. Get well soon, Harry!

— FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) November 20, 2026

"However, no excuses. I think it was a fair result and that Koln deserved to take the point.

"We have other things to worry about, I must admit. Without complaining too much, we must accept what we're in for and regain our strength so that we can get results in the next few matches despite the odds.

"It's an extremely unusual situation at the moment. We need incredible performances from players who aren't used to this pressure at FC Bayern. But that's just how it is.

"We'll all try to turn this situation into something positive. FC Bayern do that again and again, and that's what we want to achieve now too."

While Bayern currently sit top of the table, with 22 points from 10 matches, they are playing their weakest Bundesliga season in four years; they had only 19 points at this stage in 2022-23.

They have now gone two consecutive home games without a win (D2), though they remain unbeaten in all competitions this season (W11 D6).

Bayern could lose top spot this weekend, however, if Borussia Dortmund beat Borussia Monchengladbach on Saturday.

#1805. Super Mario! Dons hand rebuild job to Swiss success story Frick

Published: 14:14 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:45 EST, 15 November 2026

Aberdeen have appointed former Liechtenstein international Mario Frick as their new head coach.

The 52-year-old will take charge at Pittodrie, subject to the completion of UK visa formalities, following a successful spell with Swiss side FC Luzern.

Frick arrives in the north-east after five years in charge of Luzern, where he transformed the club’s fortunes after taking over in December 2021 with the team rooted to the bottom of the Swiss Super League. He guided them away from relegation trouble before leading them to a fourth-place finish and qualification for European football.

Announcing the appointment, Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington said the club had undertaken an extensive recruitment process before selecting Frick as the man to lead the Dons forward.

Bevington said: 'We are delighted to welcome Mario Frick and his assistant coach Roman Matter to Aberdeen Football Club.

'Mario has significant experience as a head coach and has delivered impressive results with both Vaduz and Luzern. He has a proven track record of building competitive teams and developing young players.

'Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team.'

Sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel also welcomed the appointment and believes Frick has the qualities to make a major impact at Pittodrie.

Pfannenstiel said: 'Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play. He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.

Aberdeen have appointed Mario Frick as their new manager

'We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I’m convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact.'

Before his spell with Luzern, Frick managed FC Balzers and FC Vaduz, winning promotion to the Swiss Super League with the latter. Across almost 290 senior matches as a head coach, he built a reputation for developing young talent, handing top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players.

As a player, Frick represented clubs including FC Basel, FC Zürich, St Gallen, Grasshopper, Siena and Ternana. A striker who could also operate in defence, he won 125 caps for Liechtenstein between 1993 and 2016 and remains his country’s record goalscorer with 16 international goals.

Frick said: 'I’m excited to be joining Aberdeen FC. It’s a club with a proud history, passionate supporters and big ambitions.

'Together with the staff, my aim is to create an environment where the players can thrive, develop and perform at their very best, while working towards our goals as a team.'

Frick and assistant coach Matter are expected to arrive in Aberdeen at the start of the week and will begin preparations for next weekend’s Premiership clash with Kilmarnock.

#1804. Standings, highs, lows, key players: How Milan Futuro, Primavera and Women have started 2026-27

The second international break of the season is upon us, which is a good time to take stock of how things are going beyond he men’s first team.

An ownership and management should not just be judged on one area of the club, but rather multiple different departments. The youth sector needs to be developing players in the right way, while the rising prevalence of women’s football gives added impetus to make the Femminile side as competitive as possible.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

That being said, can be hard enough keeping up with how the senior team are doing without thinking about the various other sides operating under the Milan umbrella. So, we have provided a summary of how Milan Futuro, Milan Primavera and Milan Women are doing so far in 2026-27.

It was all change over the summer for the Futuro as they brought in Sergio Navarro as the head coach. The idea was to create some continuity with Ruben Amorim’s more continental style of football, and the pedigree that the Spaniard has suggested it was a positive move.

While not a necessity, the objective for the campaign will no doubt have been set as competing for promotion back to the third tier, which is the level that the project started at prior to the relegation in 2024-25.

Position: It is a case of so far, so good for Navarro’s men. They sit fourth in the standings with 23 points from 11 games, obtained through seven wins, two draws and two losses. They have scored 21 goals (third-most in the league) and allowed 15.

Importantly, the Futuro have a game in hand on the sides above them. If they win it they would go level with Chievo Verona (yes, that Chievo) and Nibbiano & Valtidone who are on 26 points. The former, however, have a 10 better goal difference.

The U23s are part of the Premier League International Cup and they got past Everton 2-1 in the first game, with matches against Stoke later this month and Tottenham in November to come, both away from home.

High point: On October 18, Milan’s second team went to the current league-leaders Chievo and beat them 2-1, with Bonomi scoring a late winner. That was an early marker of what this team are capable of. A special mention must go to the Premier League Cup win at Goodison Park against Everton, too.

Low point: That aforementioned win in Verona came in the round after Milan had lost 2-1 at home to Rovato Vertovese. They are a side that have only won twice all season and currently occupy the relegation spots, so it was a big blow before a big response.

Key players: There have been multiple players that have stood out. Levin Asanji has scored four goals in the league, as has Lorenzo Ossolo. Fabio Pandolfi has been playing a deeper midfield role and looks to have quality well beyond his 18 years of age, with three goals to his name.

Silvano Vos is having a resurgence, while the likes of Emanuele Sala, Mattia Cappelletti, Alessandro Bonomi and Emanuele Borsani have all started every single game, aiding their development under the new coach. El Hadji Malick Cisse – a January arrival – is also turning a lot of heads.

For a bit more deeper reading on the tactical approach used by Milan Futuro under Navarro, we suggest reading the analysis we put out over the international break.

The 2025-26 season was a mixed one for the Primavera side, as their record of 11 wins and 11 defeats in 38 games shows perfectly. They finished 11th, nine points off the relegation play-offs but 10 points off the Scudetto play-offs, though a lot of the younger talents had been again accelerated into the Futuro side.

Giovanni Renna remained at the helm going into the new campaign, the coach that has been promoted up the ranks and thus knows a lot of the players. The hope was that continuity would yield better results, and so far it has.

Position: At the time of writing, the U20 side are sixth in the Primavera 1 league, which puts them in a final play-off spot. They have won five of their first 10 games but they have also lost four, so they remain a bit of a rollercoaster ride of inconsistency.

Looking upwards, Parma are currently top on 21 points, but the Rossoneri are within striking distance of Inter, who are in second on 19 points. However, Renna’s side are also a bad round away from being in the bottom half too.

Milan Primavera progressed in the Coppa Italia Primavera at the end of October, beating Catanzaro 2-1 thanks to a late winner from Dotta. Como are the opponents in the next round.

High point: It’s hard to look past the last two rounds in truth. The Primavera seem to have really clicked, scoring 10 goals in the last 180 minutes of action, beating Monza 5-0 away from home and then AlbinoLeffe 5-1 at home.

An honourable mention must go to the 2-0 win over Juventus in September, given they are in a similar position with also having a B-team (Juve Next Gen), so they will continue to serve as a useful point of comparison.

Low point: Back on October 10, the young Diavoli lost 2-0 against Atalanta which was their third league defeat in a row. There was talk of crisis mode as the slide down the table continued, and against an Atalanta side that are now third-bottom of the league. Thankfully, they turned it around quickly.

Key players: A bit like with the Futuro, the goals have been shared around the Milan Primavera squad. Mattia Zaramella has emerged recently as a star with four goals, as has Max Anastasio who arrived from Bologna and has the same amount.

Then, Andrea Cullotta (a centre-back), Vincent Ibrahimovic (a midfielder) and Edoardo Tartaglia (a full-back) all have two goals. Renna has called upon the same core group of players largely. Matteo Geroli, Francesco Domnitei, Cullotta, Zaramella, Tartaglia, Anastasio and Yanis Massaouadi have all appeared in every round.

Last season was not one that Milan Women will want to shout about, given that they finished sixth in the table and seven points off the play-off spots in the end. They won just nine of 22 games, placing them below even Fiorentina and Lazio, plus Juventus, city rivals Inter and eventual champions Roma.

However, like with the Primavera, consistency was the name of the game. So, Suzanne Bakker remained as the head coach, and there wasn’t as much player turnover as in some recent years.

Position: There have only been seven rounds so far in Serie A Femminile, but the Rossonere have got off to a stuttering start. They have just seven points from their opening seven games, which puts them in eighth place in the table. They have scored 11 goals but let in a joint-league-high 16.

Looking upwards, Roma lead the way with 21 points having won every game. Inter are second on 16 points – so nine more than Milan – while Juventus occupy the final play-off spot on 12. Over their shoulders, Sassuolo are in bottom (the only relegation spot), with three points.

In the Women’s Cup, Milan drew 1-1 with Como, beat Como 1907 (affiliated with the men’s team currently in Serie A, the others are a stand-alone club) 2-1, and then lost 1-0 to Juventus to end their campaign.

High point: This one is quite an easy pick, and it has to be the 2-1 victory over Juventus last month. Thea Kyvåg and Monica Renzotti overturned Lenzini’s opener, which had come with just under a quarter of an hour left on the clock, engineering a late comeback that sparked jubilant scenes.

Low point: The tone for what has been a disappointing campaign so far for Bakker’s ladies was set in round one, when they were beaten 4-1 by Como 1907. Then, losing 1-0 away at Como was another dark day, given they have only won twice.

On November 7, the 3-0 derby defeat to Inter – which included a red card for Milan – served only to highlight the big gulf between the two teams at the moment.

Key players: Christy Grimshaw remains the shining light for Milan Women, with three goals and an assist to her name. The scoring charts then see Sara Stokic on three goals, with Sara Fornes, Park Soojeong and Monica Renzotti all netting twice.

Grimshaw is one of three players to start every game so far under Bakker, with the others being defenders Angelica Soffia and Nerea Nevado. Sandra Estevez has emerged as the number one between the sticks too.

#1803. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners 'keen to sign' Brentford attacker in January

By Saikat Mandal | 20 Nov 2026 12:45, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:11

Arsenal reportedly remain interested in signing Brentford attacker Kevin Schade during the January transfer window.

Bolstering the left-wing position, along with bringing in a new striker, are priorities for Mikel Arteta, and several players have been linked with a move to the Emirates Stadium in recent weeks.

Schade joined the Bees in January 2023 and has since made 118 appearances for the club, scoring 25 goals.

The German attacker has made 10 Premier League appearances this season, starting nine of them, and has scored three goals so far.

According to TEAMTalk, Arsenal view Schade as a strong candidate to add depth and competition across their forward line.

Schade is primarily a left-sided forward but possesses the versatility to operate across the frontline, a quality that appeals to Arteta.

The winger is regarded as a realistic and proven Premier League option for the Gunners, given his ability to make an immediate impact.

While Arsenal's interest is genuine, any potential move would depend on Brentford's valuation and how Schade's contract negotiations with the club progress.

Schade has entered the final two years of his Brentford contract, and the club have reportedly opened talks with the player over a new deal.

The Bees are said to be keen to offer him a new long-term contract on improved terms, underlining his growing importance in Keith Andrews's squad.

The Gunners could face competition from Premier League rivals Liverpool, who have reportedly emerged as serious contenders in the race for Schade.

Arsenal are also said to be keeping tabs on RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa, although they would need to pay a substantial transfer fee to prise him away from the German club.

#1802. Jamal Musiala and Dayot Upamecano have release clauses in Bayern contracts

According to Sky Sport Germany, a previously undisclosed release clause in Jamal Musiala’s contract has become a topic of internal discussion at Bayern Munich. Although the Germany international signed a long-term deal running until 2030, the report states that a release clause can be activated as early as the summer of 2027.

Musiala is apparently not the only senior Bayern player with such a provision. Dayot Upamecano is also said to have a release clause in his contract, which would reportedly become active from 2027 and is set at €65 million.

Musiala’s situation has even been discussed at supervisory board level in recent weeks. Internal conversations are reportedly centred on the balance between his salary and sporting output. The 23-year-old said to be among the club’s highest earners on a package worth around €25 million gross per year, including bonuses, while enduring a difficult period after spending time on the sidelines through injury and other health-related setbacks.

However, despite speculation generated by the leaked contract details, there are currently no signs of an imminent departure from Bayern. Instead, Musiala’s focus is said to be on returning to full fitness and re-establishing himself as one of the leading figures for the Bundesliga champions.

#1801. Cardinale admits Milan’s NBA Europe project could be worth €5B+: “Hottest market in Europe”

Gerry Cardinale spoke at a conference last night and it’s clear that the AC Milan owner has a lot to say on the NBA Europe matter.

The NBA Europe project has been discussed for some time now, but there has been little movement. As reports have suggested, Milan were one of the first brands/clubs to throw their hat into the ring and that interest has never died.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Now, it seems that some progress could be made with the plans to develop the San Donato land into an arena. However, it still feels like we are a way away from seeing an NBA team in Milano.

Speaking at the SBJ Dealmakers conference, Cardinale sat alongside the NBA Deputy Commissioner and discussed the ongoing discussions about a new European league, as MilanNews relays from Gazzetta dello Sport.

“We will continue on our path with or without an agreement because we know that in the end, we will be the ones left standing. I honestly cannot understand how we can operate for 26 years and not be able to make a profit.

“Adam Silver and Mark Tatum [who sat alongside him] are doing everything they can to reach an agreement, but it takes two people to compromise. I am convinced that in the end, the NBA will prevail.”

The American also discussed the position that Milan are in and the future of the basketball arm of the club.

“Milan is currently the hottest market in Europe. When I arrived four years ago, I had two goals, besides winning: one was the stadium, which will finally be built, and the other was to invest in basketball.

“In fact, I had conversations with Olimpia Milano well before the advent of NBA Europe. Where will NBA Europe be in 10 years? Let’s say that if the new NBA franchise in Las Vegas is valued at $13-14 billion, I think that in 10 years, NBA Europe clubs will be worth at least half that.”

#1800. Goalkeeper scores one of the most bizarre own goals EVER during play-off clash in Argentina

Published: 14:49 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:54 EST, 15 November 2026

Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored perhaps the most bizarre own goal ever during his side's recent Primera B play-off game.

Comunicaciones were taking on Arsenal Sarandi at the weekend with the score 0-0, and the goalkeeper had caught the ball from a cross with the aim of getting the game back under way.

As he tried to throw the ball out, though, he got it all wrong and ended up launching the ball into his own net.

Bacher, 30, essentially failed to let go of the ball at the right time, leaving his team-mates stunned.

The player himself covered his face with his hand before retrieving the ball to get play started again.

Arsenal players wheeled off in celebration, only for Comunicaciones to level things up in the game soon after. Arsenal, though, scored again, and eventually won 3-2 in the first leg of the tie.

"Están matando al fútbol"Por el "insólito" gol en contra que se hace el arquero de Comunicaciones ante Arsenal. pic.twitter.com/GLUJlcKPXK

Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored a bizarre own goal during his side's third-tier play-off game

The 30-year-old failed to release the ball from a throw and launched the ball into his own net

Fans flooded to social media to react to the scarcely believable own goal.

One wrote on X: 'Haha, those who think it's because of betting. That's the level of Argentine football.'

Another posted: 'RIP Argentinian football.'

A third shared: 'The Arsenal lot celebrating... you've got some nerve.'

Bacher joined the club at the start of last year, but has always played in his homeland of Argentina.

His Comunicaciones side finished ninth in their league group of Primera B, the third tier of Argentinian football, and were taken on by an Arsenal side that came second.

They will face off in the return leg next Saturday.
