#1740. Man United CEO Omar Berrada says Red Devils did "absolutely everything" in a bid to keep wonderkid JJ Gabriel

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 15:06, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 15:09

Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada has insisted that the club did "absolutely everything" in a bid to prevent JJ Gabriel from leaving.

The 16-year-old recently posted a farewell message to Man United ahead of his expected move to Spanish giants Real Madrid.

JJ Gabriel informed Man United in September of his desire to seek pastures new, just one month before he was expected to pen scholarship terms at Old Trafford.

A professional contract was then expected to follow a year later, but JJ Gabriel's representatives informed Man United that the youngster would be looking to leave the club.

Man United have now lost a player regarded to be a generational talent, but Berrada has said that the club did "absolutely everything" in a bid to keep him.

"We did everything. Absolutely everything," Berrada told Sky Sports News when asked about JJ Gabriel's departure.

"Let's not forget with JJ, he's a very young boy with a lot of media attention around him. Our primary concern is his well-being.

"Credit to the academy and people that have been here for many years, they helped him in his development. We still think this is the best place for him to continue his career and to grow.

"This club has a very rich history and tradition of developing young players and giving them the opportunity, as we're seeing this season with Shea Lacey.

"Obviously, Kobbie Mainoo has been doing well for us for a few years now - we're not afraid of giving young players opportunities.

"Obviously, him and his family have taken the decision to leave. We can only wish him the best. We want players that want to be here, that feel being at Manchester United is a privilege."

JJ Gabriel made his senior debut for Man United in their pre-season game against Atletico Madrid during the summer, but he has departed without making a competitive appearance for the Red Devils at first-team level.

The attacker scored 29 goals and registered four assists in 32 appearances for Man United Under-18s, in addition to two goals and two assists in two appearances for Man United Under-21s in Premier League 2.

JJ Gabriel technically still has a deal with Man United's academy until the end of the season, but the teenager has a European passport through both of his parents, so a FIFA loophole could allow him to become a Real Madrid player from January.

Real Madrid have allegedly already mapped out a pathway for JJ Gabriel into their first team in the near future.

#1737. Arsenal 1-0 Hull: Not efficient, but enough

In yesterday’s preview blog, I spoke about Arsenal’s attacking efficiency, and how that might be key to taking all three points. In yesterday’s game against Hull, Arsenal took 21 shots, 10 of which were on target, and scored one goal from that. Efficient?

Despite generally dominating possession, I thought there was a lack of precision in certain aspects of our first half play. Passes weren’t quite quick enough or accurate enough, but there were moments when we could have found the breakthrough. Gabriel almost got on the end of a Noni Madueke cross which was flicked on towards the back post, Rice had a tame shot from a free kick before a late header which he probably should have done better with.

And then there was Kai Havertz. It’s fair to say Hull didn’t leave a lot of room behind a defensive line that often had six players stretched across it, but late in the half a superb Martin Odegaard pass sent him clean through, one on one with the keeper. I haven’t seen replays but in real time I felt like he should have pulled the trigger – instead he over-complicated it. You have to be prepared to shoot from there, even if it’s on your wrong foot.

Then there was a penalty incident when he complained vociferously, play went on, the ref was then told to go to the screen and we all assumed it would be a penalty. However, the ref said it was a foul but Havertz was offside – and it felt like a massive waste of time. Afterwards, it emerged it should have been a penalty, but apparently the rule is ‘open to interpretation’. So clear as mud then.

In the second half, we seemed to play down our right a lot, with Madueke the outlet most of the time. I thought he did pretty well, much better than Christos Tzolis on the other side, but the breakthrough wouldn’t come. Mikel Merino replaced Rice (who seemed to be on the end of a wild challenge in midfield that the ref just ignored as he tumbled through the air), and Viktor Gyokeres came on for Havertz.

On 71 minutes though, we found the goal. Madueke’s shot was spilled by the keeper, Odegaard was quickest to react to poke the ball home for 1-0. And to be fair, you always felt confident that would be enough. We are the masters of the single goal margin win, and this was another one. Not a day that will live long in the memory or anything, but a 1-0 win that takes us into the Interlull in really good shape, and there’s not much arguing with that.

Or really, much more to say about this game. Mikel Arteta sounded happy enough, saying:

I’m delighted with the win. To go into the international break with a win is one of the best things about being a coach or player, I would say. Regarding the performance, I thought we were the better team, had enough chances to score and make it bigger for ourselves and we weren’t efficient enough to take them.

We then had to rely on generating volume, plenty of persisting until we finally broke them down. Martin then got the goal. Not the most beautiful one, but the most effective one, a simple ‘shoot and then follow the next action’, and that was ultimately enough to win the game.

So Arsenal sit top of the table, with 9 wins from 10 so far this season in the league, and it’s a very impressive run of form. Do I wish we had more attacking potency? Absolutely, and I do worry a bit that it might bite us in the arse somewhere down the line, but for now, we can see that this is a team that just knows how to win, and perhaps that’s the most important thing.

Right, I’m gonna leave it there for this morning. I have to head back to Dublin today. It was great to see lots of you over the weekend, until next time! And we’ll have an Arsecast Extra for you tomorrow too.

#1736. England deliver the spectacular as Three Lions strip world champions Spain of their invincibility and give Thomas Tuchel the proof that his coaching IS working, writes OLIVER HOLT

Published: 17:02 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 04:59 EST, 16 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel had said he wanted evidence. He needed to believe his coaching was working. He needed to see something that told him he could help England overcome those DNA deficiencies he had identified in the aftermath of the devastating World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina.

He needed a glimpse of his England team closing the gap to the best. He needed to cling on to the idea that they could overhaul Spain, that the work he was doing could improve England so much they could win the European Championship in 2028 and end this country’s cursed cycle of despair.

Proof of concept, he called it on Saturday night when England arrived in Madrid. ‘This will be proof of concept on the highest level,’ Tuchel predicted. ‘It's the biggest test in world football. Spain seems unbeatable but we are trying to take it away from them. We are up for something spectacular.’

Something spectacular is what Tuchel promised and something spectacular is what both he and England delivered. Spain had not lost for 43 matches, a world record, but number 44 was beyond them. For just over an hour, England destroyed them. They outplayed them. They stripped them of their invincibility.

And then, when Elliot Anderson was sent off after 63 minutes for pulling back Lamine Yamal, and Spain stormed back into the game, England somehow managed to hold on for a momentous victory in the screaming, yelling cauldron of the Metropolitano. This was proof alright. This was proof positive.

Sure, it was nervy for half an hour. And, yes, England nearly found a way to throw it away. But the way they played when it was 11 v 11 was enough for any England fan to believe that England under Tuchel can climb back to the summit of a major tournament and gaze down on a view they have not seen for 60 years.

England recorded a famous victory over Spain in Madrid as they won a five-goal thriller

Elliot Anderson's red card opened the door for the world champions to mount a comeback

James Trafford made a superb double save in stoppage time to preserve England's lead

Yes, this was a Nations League dead rubber because both teams were already guaranteed progress to the quarter-finals next March, but there was no mistaking its wider significance. This was proof England are good enough to turn away from the trail of tears that has been their path for so long. Before the game, Spain had held the World Cup aloft again as one final reminder of England’s failure but by the end, by the time goalkeeper James Trafford had added to the drama with a miraculous double save, the glory and the 3-2 triumph was England’s.

Spain had won their last 12 matches in succession and the sport’s last two major tournament. They had not been beaten since March 2024 and had not lost at home since September 2022. England ended that run with 10 men. What a night. It was a special kind of crazy.

England had celebrated Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph and caps record at Wembley last week but Spain took things a stage further before the game. The boys who won the U15 World Cup were introduced to the crowd. Then the World Cup itself was carried on for goalkeeper Unai Simon to hold aloft.

England ignored it all. They started the game like an express train. They nearly took the lead inside the first two minutes when Jude Bellingham met a corner from Declan Rice on the edge of the six-yard-box and was only denied by a brilliant reaction save from Simon. Gordon’s follow-up was destined for the bottom corner before it was blocked by a Spain defender.

Spain were rattled. The crowd whistled. England forced their opponents into mistake after mistake at the back. From one of those successful presses, Kane drilled a shot inches wide. Gordon, who has made such a fine start to his Barcelona career, revelled on the stage and caused right back Marc Pubill all manner of anxieties.

Spain could barely break out of their own half but when they did, after a quarter of an hour, Yamal ran at Lewis Hall and nutmegged him before Rice chopped the teenager down. Rice was booked by French referee Clement Turpin and Lamal windmilled his hands in the air to wind up the crowd.

Pubill was replaced midway through the half. It looked like an injury but it could have been hurt pride or twisted blood. Gordon had barely given him a moment’s rest. In fact, Gordon was tireless. He harried Martin Zubimendi off the ball with ease and almost set up a chance for Bellingham.

England got the goal they deserved a minute before half-time. The build-up was controversial. Anderson played a fine through ball to Kane that doubled as a crunching tackle on Marc Cucurella. Cucurella went down as if he had been shot, which is what Cucurella always does.

Ben White slotted the ball through the keeper's legs after a brilliant England move

Harry Kane celebrates goal No 93 for England after giving them the lead from the penalty spot

The referee allowed play to continue. Kane advanced on goal and turned inside Pau Cubarsi, Spain’s brilliant young defender. Cubarsi brought him down and the referee pointed to the spot. Cucurella still lay prone. Bellingham, his Real Madrid teammate, leaned over him and told him what he thought of him.

There were a whole host of VAR checks but England passed all of them. The crowd whistled their distaste. Kane missed a penalty in the Wembley game between these two teams in September but he did not miss this one. Simon guessed the right way but Kane hit it too fiercely and it bulged the back of the net. It was his 93rd goal for England.

Spain are not used to being bossed around like this. Tempers flared after the whistle blew for half-time. Ben White and Fabian Ruiz joined in a disagreement of some sort and soon there was a flurry of pushing and shoving. It stopped short of being a melee but it was obvious Spain were shaken.

Eight minutes into the second half, England went further ahead. Rice swung a corner into the centre of the box and, as the usual wrestling match unfolded, Ezri Konsa ran in gloriously unmarked and nodded the ball down and past the helpless Simon from close range.

Four minutes later, against a general backdrop of disbelief, England were three ahead. What a goal it was, too. Bellingham, who had been his usual superhuman self, muscled his way free in the centre and fed the ball out to Kane.

Kane held the ball up and played it back to Bellingham on the edge of the box. Bellingham spotted the overlapping run of White and found him with a clever pass. White took a touch and slotted the ball past Simon. It was the Arsenal full-back’s first competitive England start, too. Maybe now England fans will stop booing him.

This was the night Thomas Tuchel had been crying out for as he got the evidence he demanded

Ezri Konsa met Declan Rice's set-piece to plant an unstoppable header in the back of the net

But then, midway through the half, England gave Spain a lifeline. Jarell Quansah was caught in possession by Yamal and as Yamal bore down on goal, Anderson pulled him back. Anderson was shown a red card and Spain were awarded a penalty. Oyarzabal waited for Trafford to commit himself and then stroked the ball into the opposite corner.

The atmosphere in the stadium was transformed. Spain sensed vulnerability in England for the first time. Fifteen minutes from time, they pulled another goal back. Yamal sprinted away down the right and slid the ball into the middle for substitute Nico Williams, who sidefooted it past Trafford.

Now, it was like the Alamo. Yamal tormented England. Trafford dived at full length to push away one of his shots and then got down at his near post to divert a shot that was creeping in. White produced another of the moments of the night with a flying block to keep out a goalbound shot from Williams.

Spain threw everything at England but England would not yield. When Trafford made that double save, everyone knew. It was to be England’s night. Tuchel had his proof of concept.

#1735. Juventus vs Venezia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 20 Nov 2026 15:24, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 15:27

Set to clash in Serie A's Sunday lunchtime slot, fallen giants Juventus and promoted strugglers Venezia will meet in Turin this weekend.

Having limped into the international break, Juve currently trail Italy's top six, while their Venetian visitors are stuck inside the drop zone despite finally posting a second win of the season.

Though Juventus are on track to reach the Europa League's knockout phase without needing a playoff, domestic results have been below par for several months.

After missing out on Champions League qualification at the bitter end of last season, the Bianconeri sit seventh in Serie A and are lacking the consistency required to mount a title charge.

Remarkably, Juve have gone 10 league games without consecutively recording the same result, and they signed off for the international break with a run of one defeat, one win and one draw.

Having lost 2-0 to Genoa, before beating Napoli by the same scoreline in Turin, Luciano Spalletti's side had to fight back twice to salvage a 2-2 draw with Fiorentina last time out.

Ahead of Thursday's Europa League game and next week's clash with high-flying Como, they must avoid another slip-up when Venezia come to town.

A former coach of Sunday's visitors, Spalletti is under heavy pressure, and he will only be able to celebrate his 600th Serie A match as a manager if Juventus claim maximum points.

History suggests that the hosts should prevail, as Venezia have lost 11 of their 14 top-flight away games against Juve, while drawing the other three.

In fact, the Lagunari's last victory against the Bianconeri anywhere dates back to a home success in April 1962.

This time, they will head to Turin under survival specialist Davide Nicola, who recently replaced promotion-winning boss Giovanni Stroppa.

Though Nicola's new side impressively upset Napoli in his first match, they subsequently lost three times without scoring, ahead of a big relegation six-pointer against Udinese.

Sending Stadio Penzo into raptures, Kike Perez scored a stunning goal that separated the pair in a tense 2-1 home win for Venezia, lifting them above their hapless visitors and off the foot of the table.

However, the Arancioneroverdi have yet to pick up any points on the road, while Nicola has previously suffered seven straight defeats in his managerial head-to-head with Spalletti.

Though Juventus still have a long injury list, full-backs Zeki Celik and Andrea Cambiaso have returned to full training and are both in contention to start.

Francisco Conceicao is also back in the fold, but Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Pierre Kalulu, Kamil Grabara, Nico Gonzalez and captain Manuel Locatelli are all unavailable.

Set to start up front, Nick Woltemade finally scored his first Serie A goal against Fiorentina; like strike partner Randal Kolo Muani, he has fared better in this season's Europa League.

After posting three goal involvements from his last two matches, Kolo Muani will hope to continue that form this weekend.

Meanwhile, French wing-back Antoine Hainaut and Nigeria striker Akor Adams are Venezia's joint-top scorers with just two league goals, and the Lagunari have Serie A's lowest shot conversion rate (5.4%).

Either Lion Lauerbach or John Yeboah should partner Adams, the visitors' club-record signing.

Fellow forward Andrea Adorante returned from a layoff during the break, but Marin Sverko and Bartol Franjic are still sidelined.

Vicario; Celik, Bremer, Lucumi, Cabal; Luiz, Koopmeiners; Kolo Muani, McKennie, Alajbegovic; Woltemade

Stankovic; Halhal, Moreno, Jesus; Hainaut, Perez, Basic, Sohm, Mazzocchi; Yeboah, Adams

The pressure is all on Juventus, who have consistently frittered away points with weak defending and wayward finishing.

Even so, the hosts should have too much nous and skill for a Venezia side that face an improbable fight for survival.

#1734. Strops, scruff, and chaos

I watched Man Utd v Aston Villa last night. When Villa conceded late on to let a two goal lead slip for the second time in the game, Unai Emery threw a strop and went down the tunnel. It’s not the first time he’s eschewed a handshake with the opposition manager, and his post-game interview where he insisted he thought the game was over was very funny because it was such obvious bullshit.

This is someone who has managed over 1000 games in his career. I’m pretty sure he knows when the final whistle blows and when it doesn’t. Can you imagine if Mikel Arteta did that? You wouldn’t be able to move for all the opinion pieces about what a sore loser he is and all the rest. But perhaps Emery gets a pass because he is ‘the best manager in the league’. Anyway, perhaps it provides a stay of execution for Michael Carrick at Man Utd, which can only be a good thing.

Meanwhile, it looks as if Pierre Sage is gonna get fired by Crystal Palace and replaced by Thomas Frank. That seems a sensible appointment to me. Enough time has passed since his spell at Sp*rs for the toxins to wear off, and he’s clearly a good manager. I’ve never been convinced by Sage, I just think he looks too scruffy. As if someone got a 10 year old to draw man and brought it to life.

I quite enjoyed this quote from Mikel Arteta in his post-game press conference after Saturday’s 1-0 win over Hull:

Sometimes we try to score the perfect goal against low blocks, but we need to be much more chaotic than that. If we open the scoring much earlier also, it changes the game.

I love it as a concept, adding some chaos to our control makes a lot of sense, but it also kinda seems at odds with what the manager asks of his players. Maybe he just means more shots from distance, maybe riskier pass when we’re trying to break the opposition down, or maybe there’s something he’s got cooking for over the Interlull and when we return we see something we never expected. He did kick the shit out of a dugout chair on Saturday, that’s a new enough development to be fair.

I wonder was he referring to the Kai Havertz chance in the first half, when he could have shot on his right foot but tried to cut back/lay it off. If you shoot, maybe you don’t score but as we saw with the winning goal from Martin Odegaard, it might end up in the path of another Arsenal player who can finish it off. Perhaps too there’s a bit of a through line between being more chaotic and what Noni Madueke is doing at the moment. He can be a bit scattergun, but as Nick Wright points out on Sky Sports, his numbers are improving. I don’t think Arteta will ever embrace full chaos, all the time, but if he can add a little more to the mix, it could certainly help.

Right, I have to leave it there for this morning. A bit shorter than normal, I know. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

The pod should be out around around lunchtime. Until then, have a good one.

#1731. FC Twente vs Willem II - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 20 Nov 2026 15:36, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:58

Two teams at opposite ends of the Eredivisie table meet on Sunday as FC Twente welcome Willem II to De Grolsch Veste

The hosts are aiming for a fourth consecutive win in this fixture to remain within touching distance of their title rivals, while the visitors are desperate for a victory to spark what has been an underwhelming campaign so far.

Twente’s 2-2 draw against Ajax just before the break saw their four-game winning run come to an end, but given they were 2-0 down midway through the second half, securing a share of the spoils resoundingly feels like a point earned rather than two lost.

Just two points behind current leaders PSV Eindhoven, John van den Brom’s side remain firmly in the title race. While they trail Feyenoord, PSV, and Ajax in goals scored, they boast the league's best defence with just 12 goals conceded, and only Heerenveen have kept more clean sheets.

Three weeks after recording their largest-ever win - a 9-0 thrashing of SBV Excelsior - the Tukkers have a chance to lay down another marker against the division’s bottom club. Given rising expectations, a victory here feels almost non-negotiable.

On a personal note, Van den Brom will also want to preserve his impressive record against this weekend’s opposite number; across their previous 11 meetings, the Twente boss has recorded seven wins and four draws.

After winning each of their first home league matches this term, Sunday’s hosts have collected just one point from their last two outings and now seek to avoid going three straight Eredivisie matches in Enschede without a win for the first time since April 2025.

Willem II ended a run of six consecutive league defeats with a 1-1 draw against PEC Zwolle on November 6, but their wait for a first victory continues, as the appointment of Jurgen Streppel has yet to yield the desired turnaround.

Streppel returned for a second spell to replace John Stegeman, who managed just two points from a possible 27 over nine matches. The Zwolle stalemate was only Willem II's third point of the season, at least six fewer than any other team.

Already 12 points worse off than at this stage of their 2024-25 relegation campaign, De Superkruiken face a herculean task to avoid the drop. Upcoming fixtures against Twente and Feyenoord - two of the current top four - over the next three gameweeks only add to their challenge.

A league-high 40 goals conceded means Willem II are frequently punished for their league-low 11 goals scored. Consequently, there must be drastic improvement at one end of the pitch if they are to turn things around.

Facing a team that have scored 14 goals in the final 30 minutes of matches, Sunday’s hosts cannot afford to lose focus in a period in which they have conceded 19 goals, just under half of their season total.

Max Bruns has not featured for Twente since September and remains unavailable, one of two defenders out of contention alongside Stav Lemkin, with the Israeli international suffering a long-term injury just before the start of the season.

Twenty-year-old Filip Erik Thorvaldsen is set to miss a sixth consecutive game for the hosts, who are also still without first-choice goalkeeper Lars Unnerstall.

Wout Weghorst is one of four players tied on nine goals in the Golden Boot race, and the striker will be eager to add to his tally.

Justin Hoogma (knee) and Amine Lachkar (groin) are Willem II’s two guaranteed absentees for Sunday’s clash, with the latter sidelined since July 2025.

However, French shot-stopper Thomas Didillon could also miss out for the away side, having featured just once since mid-August.

Drommel; Van Rooy, Propper, Nijstad, Adelgaard; Zerrouki, Weidmann; Rots, Taha, Orjasaeter; Weghorst

Delanghe; Tjoe-A-On, Dekker, Stam, Ter Avest; Twigt, Zarrouk; Van Crooy, Van Aalst, Vilhena; Haen

On paper, Sunday’s fixture appears to be Twente’s easiest game of the season so far, but as has been seen on several occasions, things are rarely that straightforward.

Still, we fully expect the hosts to make light work of their visitors and cruise to all three points at the end of 90 minutes.

#1730. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw

“We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

“It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”

Cody Gakpo was linked with both Tottenham and Manchester City during the transfer window but stayed at Liverpool and has been in good form in these first three games of the season. He has assisted all three of Alexander Isak’s goals so far.

4 - Cody Gakpo has been directly involved in four goals in the Premier League this season (1 goal, 3 assists). This century, only Mo Salah in 2024-25 has had more goal involvements through Liverpool's opening three games of a league campaign (6).Retained. pic.twitter.com/hGN0NpF5A3

"He's important for us"Virgil van Dijk says Cody Gakpo will be important for Liverpool this season after the win over Ipswich 💪 pic.twitter.com/XLWfxbpK2d

“You have to believe in yourself and have the belief of the fans that you are the man when you come for that much money. He had a terrible injury last year, but you can hear the Liverpool fans. They absolutely love what they saw. Some of his skills, his movement. That comes from his goal last week and the confidence that brings. Fingers crossed he can carry this on.”

2 - Liverpool have now won as many Premier League away games by 2+ goals this season (1) as they did in the whole of last season (2-0 v West Ham in November 2025).Lift-off. pic.twitter.com/rp39p6C8z5

The Swede’s two early goals have earned Liverpool all three points at Portman Road and the travelling Liverpool fans are singing his name. Isak’s fellow teammates are pushing him towards the travelling fans to take their adulation as they belt out his name.

The final whistle goes at Portman Road and Andoni Iraola picks up his first win as Liverpool boss with a 2-0 victory thanks to Isak’s quickfire double inside the opening 10 minutes. Like they did two seasons ago, Liverpool win 2-0 at Portman Road.

Enciso has a late shot from the edge of the box but it goes wide of the far post.

McAteer shoots from range but there is not enough power to trouble Alisson, who makes the save down to his right.

A late change from Liverpool as Koumas replaces Wirtz.

Due to that VAR review for the Liverpool penalty that was not, there will probably be five or six added minutes.

Clarke’s shot from just outside the Liverpool penalty area takes a deflection off his teammate Diop and goes wide.

Davis is getting a fair bit of joy down Ipswich’s left and the ball has been on to him quite a few times. He is being afforded too much space by Liverpool to get crosses in.

Andoni Iraola is bringing on Nyoni for Mac Allister, who was on a booking.

Davis is found making a run in behind and his cross from the left side of the box is blocked by Araujo and goes behind for a corner. Lukic’s delivery is headed away at the front post by Gravenberch.

Double change for Ipswich as McAteer and Ouattara replace Fatawau and Palacios.

Barcola drives down Liverpool’s left and, as he approaches the Ipswich box, cuts onto his right and feeds it across to Gakpo, whose shot misses the target.

The ball comes to Flemming on the edge of the box and he tries to curl one into the far corner but it is an easy save for Alisson.

Barcola is nearly played in behind but Scherpen does really to get out of his goal quickly and gets to the ball first, just ahead of Barcola.

Davis and Ipswich can count themselves very, very lucky. It would have been a penalty but Szoboszlai was offside when the original ball was played. For the second time tonight, an offside call massively goes in Ipswich’s favour; one to deny Isak a hat-trick and now to deny Liverpool a penalty. A massive let-off for Ipswich.

#IPSLIV – 68'VAR recommended an on-field review for a potential penalty, but determined that Szoboszlai was in an offside position in the build-up.REF: "After review, there's a penalty shout on Szoboszlai. However, in the build-up to the penalty shout, Szoboszlai is in an… pic.twitter.com/DN4i8rj5fg

Liverpool are demanding a penalty. Szoboszlai is played in behind and is constantly having his shirt pulled by Davis. Davis then appears to bring Szoboszlai down inside the box but the referee waves it away. Davis gets none of the ball and the referee is being sent to the screen...

Barcola’s first few touches in a Liverpool shirt are pretty good down the left. He is playing in his most natural position of wide left, with Gakpo now down the middle and Szoboszlai on the right.

Gary O’Neil is going to make a double change as Clarke and Flemming come on, with the latter making his debut. Maeda and Emersonn come off.

So, here comes from the £123m Frenchman as Barcola enters the fray for his Liverpool debut. Gravenberch also comes on. There will be no first Liverpool hat-trick for Isak as he heads off, as does Munoz.

Bradley Barcola comes on to make his Liverpool debut! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/PjO78nlcqj

Andoni Iraola must be ripping his air out with the lack of composure and control from his side since half-time. It is no wonder he is about to turn to his bench and a certain Frenchman.

Enciso is given far too much space to drive towards the Liverpool box before shooting but Alisson makes the save. Liverpool, despite being 2-0 up, have showed a real lack of composure since the break.

If trends are anything to go by, Bradley Barcola will be introduced in the next three or four minutes. Andoni Iraola likes to change things around the hour mark and if the Frenchman warms up anymore, he will nearly overheat.

Kerkez is the latest player into the book for a foul on Fatawu.

Fatawu receives it out on the right for Ipswich and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before curling an effort towards the far post but it goes wide.

Jacquet takes a heavy touch from a high ball and ends up taking out Emersonn, which earns the Frenchman a booking.

Liverpool work it well down their left as Isak plays it into Gakpo, who drives towards the Ipswich box. He plays it across the face of the penalty area to Szboszblai, who flicks it first time into the path of Wirtz. The German’s effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger finds a free Mac Allister at the front post but the Argentine’s header is straight at Scherpen. That was a good chance for Mac Allister.

We are back under way at Portman Road. No changes for either side at the break.

We have just seen replays of a possible penalty shout for Liverpool right at the end of the first half for a foul on Gakpo by Fatawu and it looked a decent shout.

Possession: Ipswich 41%-59% LiverpoolShots: 8-7Shots on target: 2-6Corners: 3-2Touches in opposition box: 7-12

Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they currently protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Araujo slices a clearance out of play for an Ipswich corner. A real gift for the home side as Araujo was not under any real pressure.

Isak should head away at the near post but it comes to Mac Allister to clear away.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

Szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

Tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an important clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

Lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

Szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

Another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

Liverpool take a deserved lead at Portman Road. Kerkez wins the ball back for Liverpool on halfway and the ball comes to Gakpo. The Dutchman drives forward and spots Isak in space to his right. Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

Wirtz is penalised for a very soft foul on Enciso, who just threw his hands in the air after the slightest bits of contact. The referee Darren England was not initially going to give it but eventually does, giving Ipswich the chance to swing it in from the left into the Liverpool penalty area.

Fatawu swings it in with his left but Alisson punches away.

It has been all Liverpool in these early stages but have yet to have a shot. Ipswich have barely touched the ball thus far.

Liverpool win the first corner of the game as Davis is forced to put it behind after good work from Munoz down Liverpool’s right.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger is headed away from danger.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Portman Road and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

The Paraguayan is in his second stint at Ipswich and has two assists to his name in the first two league games.

“It gives us a big belief that we can compete at the level. Coming up from the Championship, there is always some doubt around. The home win over Sunderland was huge for us. And then to be in the game for as long as we were at Manchester United was impressive. I have challenged the lads a lot. We do not focus on the outcome or results, we just commit to being the best version of ourselves. We cannot go toe-to-toe with everyone. We have to be sensible and smart.”

Andoni Iraola has made a change at right-back tonight, with Ronaldu Araujo replacing Jeremie Frimpong. Araujo arrived at Liverpool this summer on loan with an option to buy from Barcelona.

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

Ipswich were very active in the market upon their return to the Premier League, making 14 signings in total, with plenty of them involved tonight. Here is a sample of what Gary O’Neil’s side did during the window:

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

#1729. Interlull musings and shiny distractions

We’re two days into the final Interlull of the year and, as you might expect, there’s not a huge amount going on. The senior fixtures don’t start until Thursday, so we haven’t even got a fresh batch of international press conference quotes to sink our teeth into. Slim pickings.

This time around, 20 of our 25 first-team players have been selected, which is a pretty remarkable tally. All the more so when you consider Noni Madueke can count himself unlucky to have missed out for England, while Bukayo Saka and William Saliba would ordinarily be shoo-ins.

Any concerns about the Frenchman’s absence against Hull, having travelled to Prague in midweek, were eased the following morning when he lined up for the under-21s against Aston Villa in Premier League 2. More minutes in his legs, rather than another injury to worry about.

Bolstered by Saliba and Max Dowman, whose domestic suspension kept him out of Saturday’s game, the youngsters ran out 5-2 winners. Given they’re currently 21st out of 31 teams in their Swiss-style league table, perhaps this is the way forward. Send the big guns down a level and start battering our way towards more club silverware. Relentless madman Arteta, finding new frontiers for his evil genius. He doesn’t just leave his technical area. He thinks outside it.

If you missed it, Max has been promoted to England’s under-21s for this window. He’ll join Arsenal loanees Tommy Setford and Ethan Nwaneri, as well as former Hale Enders Brooke Norton-Cuffy, who came off the bench for Hull on Saturday, and Amario Cozier-Duberry, who seems to be doing well at Middlesbrough on loan from Brighton.

Given Max has been in and around Mikel Arteta’s first team for a couple of seasons now, it’s easy to take milestones like this for granted. But playing under-21 international football at 16 is another significant step, even for someone whose talent has made rapid progress seem almost routine.

Back in September, Lee Carsley described his eventual promotion as inevitable, while stressing that the timing had to be right. The point was to bring him into a squad where he could play and compete, rather than move him up simply because everyone expected it.

Carsley referenced Nwaneri when discussing the temptation to push exceptional youngsters through the age groups. His point was that the aim is a long senior career, not winning a race to the first cap. That seems sensible enough. Max doesn’t need every appearance to become an audition for the next level.

A couple of games against Portugal and France should be a useful challenge in their own right. Carsley and Arteta also know each other from their Everton days, which ought to help when discussing what he needs.

With England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland hosting Euro 2028, you can imagine that tournament already features somewhere in Max’s ambitions. There’s plenty of football between now and then, though. For the moment, let’s see how he gets on with this next step.

Elsewhere, most of our European internationals will be occupied with the Nations League, while the South American trio rack up the air miles again. Piero Hincapie heads home to Ecuador for friendlies against Costa Rica and Bolivia, while Gabriel and Bruno Guimaraes face Japan and Singapore, both in Singapore.

I appreciate Brazil’s options are more limited when European teams are tied up with UEFA fixtures, but their friendly schedule does sometimes feel like somebody has thrown a dart at a map. No doubt the commercial logic is compelling, but that doesn’t make you any less worried about tired hamstrings.

Anyway, fingers crossed they all come back with their limbs intact.

In other news, Italian publication Tuttosport has named Andrea Berta the winner of its Best Executive Award at this year’s Golden Boy Awards. The Arsenal sporting director collects the gong three transfer windows into his tenure, the latest of which ended with some fans calling for his head after the failed pursuits of Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez.

Either the bar is pretty low, he’s basking in the reflected glory of the team’s success, or it’s one of those shindigs where buying an inordinately expensive table guarantees you something shiny to take home. The cynic in me wasn’t exactly silenced by the news that Joan Laporta won Best President and Jorge Mendes Best Agent. In fact, I snorted when I read that. And lest we forget, Edu picked up a similar award from the same organisers in 2023…

Myles Lewis-Skelly was in contention for the actual Golden Boy award, which went to Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi. Hard to argue too much with that, given the 19-year-old was at the heart of Spain’s World Cup win.

Cubarsi also made the FIFPRO World 11. More pertinently for us, so did David Raya. Having finished second to compatriot Unai Simon in the Ballon d’Or’s Best Goalkeeper category, I imagine there’s some satisfaction in getting the nod from the people who actually play the game. More than 26,000 professionals from 75 countries cast their votes, which is a fairly substantial dressing room to win over.

Alessia Russo, who is in fine form even if Arsenal Women are not, also earned her third selection for the Women’s World 11.

As you’ll have gathered from the snippiness above, I find it easy to be cynical about these things. There are so many awards now that you half expect to get one for finding your seat at the ceremony. Still, sometimes it’s nice to give people a pat on the back and recognise a job well done.

On an entirely unrelated note, have you voted for us to win Best Fan Media at the upcoming FSA Awards? You’ve only got a week left. A prestigious honour, that one. 😉

Right, I think that’s as much toothpaste as I can squeeze out of a slow news day. If anything else happens, we’ll have it covered on Arseblog News. Catch you next time.

#1728. Ashley Cole accidentally shooting a student, bare-chested Marcus Bent threatening police with a meat cleaver - and an ex-Barcelona star firing a gun in a hospital! Footballers' fascination with weapons after Amar Dedic's bow and arrows saga

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and WILL GOVE

Published: 07:00 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EST, 16 November 2026

Amar Dedic might have fancied himself as Robin Hood – but the Newcastle United defender's latest adventure in the Northumberland countryside led to a rather less merry altercation with police last week.

The Magpies star sparked a major police operation after being spotted carrying a bow and arrows near a reservoir outside Newcastle, with at least six patrol cars joining the search for the £30million player.

After tracking down and questioning the Bosnian, officers were satisfied there was no threat to the public and that the equipment was intended for recreational use.

But Dedic's escapade was certainly not the first time a footballer has found himself in hot water over the possession, carrying or use of a weapon, with brass knuckles, meat cleavers and BB guns among the bizarre arsenal of items to have attracted the authorities' attention over the years.

Marcus Bent, with a meat cleaver, in Surrey

Former Middlesbrough and Everton forward Marcus Bent was tasered in his own home by police after threatening armed police officers with a meat cleaver and kitchen knife while under the influence of cocaine.

Bent, who avoided jail in 2016 after he pleaded guilty to possession of cocaine and affray, called Surrey Police after thinking he had discovered an intruder in his home.

Officers arrived at the scene but were initially unable to gain access to the property. Guildford Crown Court heard how the officers were about to use a battering ram to gain entry when a bare-chested Bent 'flung' open the door holding two chef's knives, with his 'eyes wide, jaw clenched and his body rigid'.

Bent, who was handed a 12-month sentence, suspended for two years, later said: 'I was paranoid and I was hallucinating. I felt there were people in my house. I remember thinking the door handle was moving.

'At no point was I ever going to take someone's life. I called them because I was hallucinating, paranoid, terrified.'

Marcus Bent arrives at court before pleading guilty to possession of cocaine and affray

Ashley Cole, with an air rifle, in Cobham

To most, Ashley Cole is England's all-time greatest full-back but the three-time Premier League winner also made headlines for an infamous training ground air rifle incident.

Back in 2011 while playing for Chelsea, Ashley Cole accidentally shot and injured 21-year-old student Tom Cowan, who was on work experience at the Blues' training ground in Cobham, Surrey.

The Champions League winning left-back was reportedly 'larking about' with a .22 air rifle and accidentally shot Cowan from just five feet away.

The student had assumed he would get an invaluable experience on his brief visit to Cobham but instead had to be treated by medics and rest for the remainder of the day after the shot was fired.

Cole accidentally shot a 21-year-old on work experience at Chelsea's training ground

Ex-England star Darren Bent ran into trouble early in his career when he was questioned over the alleged shooting of a 12-year-old boy with a ball-bearing gun.

While starring for his boyhood club Ipswich at the age of 20 in May 2004, Bent was arrested on suspicion of possession of an imitation firearm with intent to cause violence, before he was placed on bail and eventually released without charge pending further investigations.

According to a Suffolk Police statement at the time, a 12-year-old boy at a play area in Kesgrave had been struck in the back by a pellet from a ball-bearing gun (BB Gun). The incident was reported to authorities by his mother.

Bent, who was given a formal caution for his actions, went on to enjoy a fruitful career in the Premier League, representing the likes of Charlton, Tottenham, Sunderland and Aston Villa while also winning 13 caps for the Three Lions.

Early on his career Premier League legend Darren Bent was arrested on suspicion of possession of an imitation firearm

Karim Adeyemi, with brass knuckles, in Germany

The only member of this list to still be playing is Germany and Barcelona's Karim Adeyemi who was fined £396,000 in 2025 for possessing a pair of brass knuckles.

The former Borussia Dortmund forward was caught with the knuckles back in 2024, at the age of 22, but had to wait until the following year to receive his punishment.

Under German law the possession, procurement and use of brass knuckles is prohibited. The young winger avoided a public trial and a criminal record and was given a fine consisting of 60 daily payments of £6,600.

Although he never used the weapon, the German was in hot water  as he briefly lost his starting place in the German national team and at Borussia Dortmund.

The Westphalia giants released a statement saying: 'BVB always takes criminal allegations seriously and uses them as an opportunity to discuss them with its employees while respecting confidentiality obligations.'

Adeyemi was lucky to dodge prison time after being charged with the possession of brass knuckles

Diego Maradona, with an air rifle, in Buenos Aires

Argentina icon Diego Maradona caused injuries to four people when he fired an air rifle at journalists and photographers while hiding behind a parked Mercedes outside his Buenos Aires home in February 1994.

Four years later, Maradona was found guilty of assault with a weapon and given a suspended prison sentence of two years and ten months, which was later reduced to an even two years.

To many he is the best of all time but Diego Maradona is hardly infallible off the pitch

Despite appealing against the sentence which they claimed was 'too light', the journalists injured by Maradona said the verdict at least demonstrated there was 'justice for all' in Argentina.

'At least this exemplary case does show that there is justice for all,' said Daniel Talamoni, one of the four reporters who sued the World Cup winner.

'When the case began four years ago, everyone said it was impossible. They would sentence a man idolised in Argentina and forgive everything.'

Arda Turan, with an unlicensed gun, in a Turkish hospital

Keen fans of European football will not need to be reminded of who Arda Turan is. But they may be surprised to learn that the former Atletico Madrid and Barcelona star has had some serious trouble with the law.

Turan somehow avoided a jail sentence after discharging an unlicensed firearm in a hospital

In 2018 while on loan from Barcelona in his home country of Turkey at Istanbul Basaksehir, Turan got into an altercation with Turkish singer Berkay Sahin, who ended in hospital with a broken nose.

Then Turan turned up at the hospital that was treating Sahin with an unlicensed firearm, and fired a shot into the floor.

He was eventually sentenced to two years and eight months behind bars for firing a gun to cause panic, illegal possession of weapons and intentional injury but the sentence was suspended for five years. Basaksehir also fined the midfielder £350,000 over the incident.

Nearly a decade after the incident, Turan now manages Ukrainian powerhouse Shakhtar Donetsk, joining the club in May of last year.

#1727. Zubimendi addresses tiredness and transfer talk

Good morning all, hope you’re well! It’s St. Martin’s Day in Germany, a day I’d never heard of until I had a child over here. Kids will leave Kindergarten and chant as they walk through their neighbourhoods with lanterns this evening, as is tradition. Doesn’t sound creepy at all, does it?

St. Martin was, as the story goes, a 4th-Century Roman soldier and is best known for sharing his cloak with a freezing beggar.

Fitting, then, that Martin Zubimendi should be linked with a move to Chelsea (and others). It would be the saintly thing to do to share some of our midfield spoils with the desperate, downtrodden, shivering squad that Xabi Alonso has at his disposal. I hope we let them get absolutely glacial – Siberian, even, given their history – and keep our glorious cloak of midfielders all to ourselves.

The first rule of the international break is, of course, to ignore all transfer rumours. Club football goes away but there are still pages to fill, newspapers to sell, online traffic to amass, and something has to fill the void.

And, speaking to Marca, the midfielder has denied that he’s unhappy:

I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation. (Not playing) is something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too.

I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side. I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very quickly.

Asked about the toll that playing so much took on him last season – Zubimendi was the only Arsenal player to play in all 38 Premier League games, he started 34 of those and had the third most minutes in the squad, behind David Raya and Declan Rice, across all competitions – he admitted that that was a factor:

I don’t like to blame everything on my physical condition, but I definitely noticed it that year. It was a new year for me, with a lot of new stimuli. I played a huge number of minutes and, to be honest, I was tired. Then there were other things too, but one of them could very well have been my physical condition.

I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season. As he does with all the players, he explained the plan to me. He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

And he completely dismissed any suggestion that he is talking to other clubs, given those links to the Madrid sides and Chelsea:

I haven’t wasted any energy on outside things. I’m busy enough trying to earn a place, get playing time, and fight to win this Premier League, which is looking so promising. I haven’t spent any energy on it, nor have I contacted anyone.

To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too. I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumours can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish. Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close (to a transfer), but not at all.

Still, I do think the case of Zubimendi is an interesting one. Having lost his place late last season, he returned late in the summer, and is yet to start a Premier League game in 2026-27 following the emergence of Myles Lewis-Skelly and the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes.

Here we have a player Arsenal desperately wanted and agreed a deal for a year ahead of signing him, would they really be looking to move him on again now that he’s spent what is essentially just a quarter of a season not as first choice? So much focus has been placed on building a squad that can sustain injuries or absences, and then we’d leave ourselves light again?

Maybe? You never can know how transfers pan out ahead of time, and things can change quickly in football but, as Zubimendi suggests, they can change quickly in the other direction again too. Did anyone, for instance, envisage Lewis-Skelly starting against Atletico Madrid just a week before it actually happened?

I do think his particular rise, and a stressful second half of the season, has clouded what we all thought of Zubimendi’s first half-season at Arsenal, and how much he contributed across the entire campaign. At this stage a year ago, we were two points worse off than we are now but still top of the league by six points, with more goals scored and fewer goals conceded than we are 10 games in this time around. He was a big part of that.

He was a huge part of winning the title and reaching the Champions League final – he started 43 of our 53 games across those two competitions. He started every Champions League knockout game up until the semi-final second leg and played all of extra-time in the final.

And if he was suffering physically, there was no break in the summer, as he went off to the World Cup, Spain went all the way, and he was back on the pitch for Arsenal (having had no pre-season) in Cardiff as we won the Community Shield, less than a month on from the World Cup final.

For all that, I can also see why someone would possibly want to make the case for moving on. Seeing a player not be used (Zubimendi has played in seven of our league games so far this season, by the way!) feels like an obvious place to upgrade, and we’ve been scarred before by letting players sit on the bench before then struggling to move them on for a fair fee.

We’re also going to need to refresh the age of the team and especially the midfield before long. When you don’t just look at the players themselves but actually account for who is playing the minutes, we have the third-oldest squad in the league this season. The frontline will need new faces soon – that’s not news to anyone – in terms of age as well as quality, but the midfield will need it on the age front as well.

We’ve also given the fewest minutes in the league to players under the age of 23 (around 6%) by some distance. If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it, but if you don’t get the balance right it will break in time.

Right now, though, this season, we’re likely to need our whole squad. We can’t be making it weaker. If one of Declan Rice – God forbid – or Bruno Guimaraes were to pick up a knock and miss a month, Zubimendi would suddenly be in line for a lot of football. Zubimendi who, again, was central to us winning the league last season.

It’s far too soon into the season to write his campaign off, especially when we saw how things changed so suddenly in that exact position back in May. Let’s see how things look when the summer rolls around, but there’s no need to rush into a decision.

Right then, have a great day all – and I’ll leave you with the gorgeous generosity of another St. Martin close to our hearts.

#1726. Real Madrid attacker agrees contract until 2031 despite starting just twice under Mourinho

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 15:39

Real Madrid are reportedly preparing to secure the future of an out-of-favour attacker with an extraordinary £880m release clause, despite his limited involvement under Jose Mourinho this season.

Morocco international Brahim Diaz is said to have agreed a new contract until June 2031, potentially extending his stay at the Santiago Bernabeu by another four years.

According to Spanish television programme El Chiringuito, the agreement includes a €1bn (£880m) release clause, with an official announcement expected next week.

Journalist Marcos Benito claims the 27-year-old signed the extension approximately two weeks ago, although Madrid have yet to confirm the arrangement publicly.

The reported deal is particularly striking given Brahim's position in Mourinho's squad, where he has struggled to secure regular opportunities despite contributing three assists this season.

His long-term future may be approaching a resolution, but his immediate prospects of becoming a first-team regular appear considerably less certain.

Brahim's existing agreement is due to expire in June 2027, making his future a subject of considerable speculation during the opening months of the campaign.

Real Madrid have been working to retain the versatile attacker, who returned from a three-year loan spell at AC Milan in 2023 and has provided valuable attacking depth in recent seasons.

However, he has found opportunities increasingly difficult to secure since Mourinho took charge.

The former Manchester City youngster has made nine appearances across all competitions in 2026-27, starting only twice and accumulating just 249 minutes of playing time.

His average of fewer than 28 minutes per appearance underlines the limited nature of his involvement, while he has started the last 11 matches on the bench.

Brahim has nevertheless contributed three assists, demonstrating that he can still influence matches during relatively brief appearances.

Competition for attacking positions has become particularly demanding.

Arda Guler has established himself as a more prominent member of Mourinho's plans, while Jude Bellingham and summer signing Yan Diomande occupy important roles in Madrid's attacking structure.

Vinicius Junior's anticipated return from suspension and Rodrygo's recovery from injury could further complicate Brahim's attempts to secure additional minutes.

The situation has already prompted questions about his future.

Earlier this month, Sports Mole reported on Brahim's prolonged spell among the substitutes and the growing concerns surrounding his lack of playing time.

Despite those difficulties, Mourinho has reportedly supported the club's efforts to retain the Morocco international.

The proposed extension would strengthen Madrid's contractual position considerably, although a release clause of €1bn should not be interpreted as a realistic valuation or asking price.

Such figures are frequently included in contracts at major Spanish clubs to provide protection against unwanted departures.

There is, however, some uncertainty surrounding the precise duration of Brahim's new deal.

While El Chiringuito reports an agreement until 2031, Spanish newspaper AS has suggested that his renewal is arranged until 2030.

Neither version has been officially confirmed by Real Madrid.

Securing a new contract would represent a significant commitment from Madrid, but it would not guarantee Brahim a more substantial role in the team.

His position is particularly intriguing given that the club have several established attacking options and continue to develop younger players competing for similar positions.

For Brahim, the challenge is to turn occasional contributions into a more consistent place in Mourinho's starting XI.

That question also has implications for Morocco, where the midfielder remains an important international despite his restricted opportunities in Spain.

The Atlas Lions are building towards the 2030 World Cup, which Morocco will co-host alongside Spain and Portugal.

National team coach Mohamed Ouahbi has previously expressed a desire to see his players become more influential at club level, while acknowledging Brahim's ability to make a difference for his country.

Former Morocco international Mustapha Hadji has taken a stronger position, publicly questioning whether such limited club involvement is compatible with regular international selection.

Brahim's reported extension therefore raises an obvious sporting dilemma.

Remaining at the Bernabeu offers the prospect of competing for major trophies and retaining his place at one of Europe's most prestigious clubs.

However, the attacking competition that has restricted him to just two starts this season is unlikely to disappear simply because his contractual future is secured.

The deal would also make a potential departure more complicated, with interested clubs likely to require negotiations with Madrid rather than having the opportunity to sign him as a free agent next summer.

There is no indication that Brahim has asked to leave, and his reported decision to extend his contract suggests that he remains committed to fighting for his place.

For Mourinho, the challenge is different: finding sufficient opportunities for a talented squad player whom Madrid appear determined to retain for the long term.

An official announcement could settle the uncertainty surrounding Brahim's contract, but his limited involvement on the pitch remains a separate issue that the new agreement cannot resolve.
